entries.title: Realm Auras
entries.summary: Auras rate how strongly a realm holds an area on a scale up to 10, usually act as a modifier on supernatural activity, and when two realms contest a place only the stronger holds sway at a time.
quotes: which can be rated in power on a scale from 1 to 10

entries.title: Realm Interaction
entries.summary: An aura modifies all supernatural activity in it according to the Realm Interaction table and adds botch dice for acts in a foreign realm.
quotes: For each point of aura rating, roll an extra botch die.

entries.title: Realm Interaction Table
entries.summary: Table of how each realm's aura modifies powers of each realm, with a worked example, and the rule that Divine powers are not hampered by other auras.
quotes: Divine powers have no penalty and no additional botch dice in auras of the other realms.

entries.title: Supernatural Activity Rolls Modified by Aura
entries.summary: Sidebar listing which rolls and totals the aura modifier applies to: casting, lab totals, supernatural Ability rolls, Magic Resistance and Penetration.
quotes: Thus, a magus in a Magic aura of 4 has a +4 bonus to his Magic Resistance, while a demon has a -4 penalty.
The aura modifier does not apply to Penetration twice.

entries.title: Magical Auras
entries.summary: Describes typical strengths and character of Magic auras, where covenants are usually sited, and the dangers of the strongest auras; Magic auras do not vary cyclically.
quotes: Most magical areas have an aura from 1 to 5.

entries.title: Divine Auras
entries.summary: Divine auras (the Dominion) are nearly ubiquitous where believers live, strengthen on Sundays and holy days, and wane at night and on evil days.
quotes: On Sundays and holy days the power of the Dominion increases; at night and on evil days it wanes.

entries.title: Sources of Divine Auras
entries.summary: Typical Divine aura strengths for fields, villages, towns, places of worship, relic sites and the holiest places.
quotes: Most places of worship have an aura of 4, while places with wider significance, such as cathedrals, important mosques, and the churches of major monasteries, have an aura of 5.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, pp.10-17

entries.title: Magic Auras (chapter introduction)
entries.summary: Introduces Magic auras, pointing to the core rules for aura effects on Hermetic magic and for Warping in strong auras, and the debate among magi about what auras are.
quotes: Auras of level six and above cause Warping according to the rules in ArM5, pages 167-168.

entries.title: Sources of Magical Auras
entries.summary: How Magic auras arise from fine natural features or from magical creatures and activity, and the usual upper limits on the strengths produced.
quotes: If a moderately powerful (Might 30 or more) magical creature takes up residence in an area, that place will, over the course of years, acquire a weak Magical aura.

entries.title: Infernal Auras
entries.summary: Describes the effects of Infernal auras on travelers and magic, that magic can detect them, and that they wax at night and wane on holy days.
quotes: Of greater concern to magi, Infernal auras interfere with the use of magic.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pp.10-17

entries.title: Sources of Infernal Auras
entries.summary: Infernal auras arise from serious or repeated sin and from infernal creatures or powers, with examples of the strengths produced.
quotes: In an area with no aura, a cruel and premeditated murder can create a level 1 aura.

entries.title: Faerie Auras
entries.summary: Faerie auras range from weak to immense and vary in strength with how closely the surroundings match the nature of the faeries within.
quotes: Faerie auras tend to vary in strength depending on how closely the surrounding world matches the nature of the faeries within.

entries.title: Sources of Faerie Auras
entries.summary: Faerie auras arise from faeries, their powers, and stories told about a place, and tend to be stronger than other aura types.
quotes: Faerie auras also arise when stories are told about a place.

entries.title: The Mundane
entries.summary: Mundane areas have no aura, so powers work there without hindrance, though most settlements share somewhat in the Dominion.
quotes: The mundane has no aura rating

entries.title: Church Auras
entries.summary: Divine auras spread from the church altar as far as the bells can be heard or to the parish boundary, with the aura level depending on the type of church or distance from it, given in a table.
quotes: Divine auras radiate from the church altar for as far as the church bells can be heard, or to the edge of the parish boundary, whichever is closer.

entries.title: The Feast of All Souls and the Dominion
entries.summary: Origin of the Feast of All Souls on 2 November, with its aura effect: on that day the Dominion is weaker than usual, Infernal auras are stronger, and some of the dead walk again.
quotes: Infernal auras increase in strength by one, and some of the dead walk once more.

entries.title: Conciatta's Glossary (aura terminology)
entries.summary: Defines the Order's standard vocabulary for describing auras: diffuse, tethered, stable, waning, waxing, existential, moral, apparent and subsumed.
quotes: An aura with no fixed sustaining source.
The strongest aura present at a given location.

entries.title: Theories Concerning Magic Auras
entries.summary: Hermetic theories about what fluid vis is and how magi's activities strengthen or weaken auras, with advice that reliably manipulating an aura should need a major breakthrough or mystery initiation and that the aura variation numbers can be changed for your saga.
quotes: Any effect that reliably manipulates a Magic aura should probably require at least a Major breakthrough or a Mystery Initiation.

entries.title: Tethers
entries.summary: A tether is the object or circumstance around which fluid vis pools to form an aura; the base aura score is built by adding the natural and preternatural tether scores.
quotes: Base Aura Score = natural aura score + preternatural aura score
Natural Aura Score (maximum 5) = sum of all natural tethers
Preternatural Aura Score (maximum 5) = strongest preternatural tether + 1 per additional tether

entries.title: Natural Tethers
entries.summary: Describes natural features (caves, forests, ice, volcanic sites, water and wind) that serve as tethers, with example descriptions for each tether score and the Warping effects they have on inhabitants.
quotes: The examples below describe only places with an aura up to a maximum score of 2

entries.title: Preternatural Tethers
entries.summary: Introduces tethers caused by mortals, magic beings or vis, which come in four types: monuments, residues, beings and vis sources.
quotes: Individual tethers may have a score up to 5

entries.title: Magic Monuments (tether)
entries.summary: Ancient buildings and constructs strongly associated with Magic act as tethers, scored by how long they have seen active use.
quotes: these places can be given one point of tether score for every full century that they have seen active use

entries.title: Magic Residues (tether)
entries.summary: Sites where extremely powerful magic left a permanent imprint can be tethers, with a score derived from the Ritual level equivalent of the magic.
quotes: (Ritual spell level equivalent of magics - 40) / 10, rounded down

entries.title: Magic Beings (tether)
entries.summary: Places inhabited by magical beings gain a tether from their Might, which fades if the being leaves or dies; death or burial sites leave a permanent tether.
quotes: has a tether score equal to (being's Might / 10), rounded down
a permanent tether equal to (being's Might / 20), rounded down

entries.title: Vis Sources (tether)
entries.summary: A source of raw vis not already in the presence of a tether can itself be treated as a tether, scored by its annual harvest.
quotes: tether score equal to (pawns harvested per year / 3), rounding down

entries.title: Aura Variation Rules
entries.summary: Explains how magical activity, vis expenditure, vis extraction and impinging foreign auras push an aura's current score above or below its base score, and how the yearly aura modifier decides whether to roll on the Strengthening or Weakening Table, with botch dice that grow with repeated fluctuation.
quotes: If the yearly aura modifier is between –3 and +3, then do nothing
every roll made on either table that results in a 9 or more causes the number of botch dice for subsequent rolls to increase by one

entries.title: Yearly Aura Modifier
entries.summary: Table of effects summed at year's end (departures from base score, impinging auras, covenant magical activity, botches, vis expenditure and extraction) to give the yearly aura modifier.
quotes: It cannot exceed +9 or be less than –9.
+3 × (base aura score – current aura score)

entries.title: Aura Strengthening Table
entries.summary: Outcome table rolled on a stress die plus the yearly aura modifier when the aura is trending stronger, ranging from no change through temporary effects and vis creation to permanent increases or a new regio level on a botch.
quotes: Roll a stress die and add the yearly aura modifier, or choose a suitable outcome.

entries.title: Aura Weakening Table
entries.summary: Outcome table for a weakening aura, mirroring the Strengthening Table with stifled magic, wasted vis, contraction, permanent loss of aura score or a regio change on a botch.
quotes: Roll a stress die and add the yearly aura modifier (ignoring the minus sign), or choose a suitable outcome.

entries.title: Symptoms of Aura Variation
entries.summary: Lists observable symptoms of a strengthening or weakening aura (inhabitants, flora and fauna, weather, mood, sentience, signs) and a rule of thumb for granting or removing supernatural abilities as the aura score changes.
quotes: one inhabitant can be (unwittingly) given a new Supernatural Virtue
a character with a Supernatural Ability loses 20 experience points

entries.title: Aligned Auras
entries.summary: Introduces rare Magic auras with a special alignment, noting that an aura has only one alignment, that detecting each alignment needs its own Intellego Vim spell, and that inhabiting higher-level aligned auras causes permanent Warping.
quotes: No aura has more than one special aspect

entries.title: Auras that Enhance Emotions
entries.summary: Emotion-enhancing auras give characters without a Magic supernatural ability a temporary new or modified Personality Trait while in the aura, scaled by aura level, with example emotions.
quotes: a temporary new Personality Trait or a modification to an existing one

entries.title: Aura Effect Table
entries.summary: Table giving the Personality Trait adjustment from an emotion-enhancing aura according to the aura's level.
quotes: | Aura Level | Personality Trait Adjustment |

entries.title: Auras Aligned with Arts
entries.summary: Art-aligned auras double the aura bonus to Casting Score and Lab Total for the matching Art, reduce Power costs for matching Might types, and remove opposed-Art penalties, with a list of Warping manifestations for each Technique and Form.
quotes: Thus, the aura modifer counts double when calculating the Casting Score.
so counts double when calculating the Lab Total

entries.title: Other Aligned Auras
entries.summary: Auras aligned to something other than an Art, such as healing, luck or distraction, which modify rolls for everyone inside according to aura strength.
quotes: Healing: Add half the aura strength (round up) to the Recovery Total for wounds or disease.

entries.title: Covenant Boons and Hooks (aligned auras)
entries.summary: Additional covenant-creation Boons and Hooks based on an aura alignment: Fine Aura, Favorable Aura and Troublesome Aura.
quotes: Fine Aura: The Magic aura of the covenant has an alignment that benefits most of those within it.

entries.title: Faerie Presence: Setting the Aura
entries.summary: How a faerie with Extend Glamour claims a place and sets its Faerie aura from its Might, what happens when two powerful faeries contest an area, and why epic sites, folklore and old monuments often carry faerie auras.
quotes: Any place that such a faerie claims with its glamour has an aura of (Faerie Might / 5).
it has an aura of 2+(highest Might/5) to a maximum of 9

entries.title: Faerie Auras Rise and Fall (Vis Extraction)
entries.summary: Foreign auras and local changes alter a faerie's Might and thus its aura; a magus who removes vis from a Faerie aura either has to deal with the faerie or lowers the aura and leaves a local hole, and the faerie may demand recompense.
quotes: the magus has effectively challenged the faerie's ownership of the area and the aura falls by 1
This hole in the aura is usually only 300 paces across

entries.title: Divine Auras in Play
entries.summary: Describes how mundane people, magi, faeries and infernal beings experience a Divine aura. Useful for adjudicating the reactions of characters who enter the Dominion or an Empyreal aura.
quotes: The Dominion auras of different faiths, such as Christianity, Islam, or Judaism, or others such as Zoroastrianism, Catharism or Gnosticism, have no different game effects.

entries.title: Conflicting Auras
entries.summary: Says how the Dominion fares against another realm's aura of equal or greater strength, with an example of a church built on a faerie site.
quotes: the Dominion will trump the opposing aura; a more-powerful aura will still overwhelm the Dominion

entries.title: Empyreal Auras
entries.summary: Explains Empyreal auras as Divine auras that arise without a congregation, from relics, saints or divine creatures, and states that they work the same as the Dominion in game terms.
quotes: There is no difference, system wise, between Empyreal auras and the Dominion.

entries.title: Empyreal Aura Power
entries.summary: How to rate an Empyreal aura from Faith Points, miracles or the lair of a divine creature.
quotes: Empyreal auras from miracles have a rating of one point for every five levels of miracle above 50.
up to a maximum rating of his Divine Might divided by 10

entries.title: Infernal Aura Strengths
entries.summary: Describes how an Infernal aura feels and what it does to people and the landscape at each band of aura strength, from subtle ill temper to Hell on earth.
quotes: Storyguides should ask for Personality rolls more frequently, to rein in these unusual impulses.

entries.title: Infernal Auras in Play
entries.summary: How an Infernal aura is centred on a focus, rises at night and on unholy days, changes on holy days in different faiths, coexists with stronger auras and erodes over time unless maintained.
quotes: All Infernal auras increase by one at night.
it takes a number of years equal to the strength of the Infernal aura for it to lose one point of strength
Whatever the source of an increase in an Infernal aura, it can never increase to a value greater than 10.

entries.title: Formation of an Infernal Aura (Corruption Roll)
entries.summary: When a major sin is committed the storyguide makes a corruption roll to create, maintain or strengthen an Infernal aura; corruption rites let diabolists deliberately attempt this. Includes a worked example.
quotes: Corruption Roll: stress die + temporary Infernal aura strength
Ease Factor (to maintain Infernal aura): 3 + dominant aura strength
Ease Factor (to increase Infernal aura): 6 + dominant aura strength
A corruption rite cannot be successfully performed more than once a season.

entries.title: Infernal Aura Examples Table
entries.summary: A table of example locations and the Infernal aura rating each would typically have, useful as a benchmark for setting aura strengths.

entries.title: Effects of an Infernal Aura
entries.summary: Dominant Infernal auras impose the normal realm-interaction modifiers on Supernatural Powers and penalise recovery rolls for wounds, diseases and deprivation injuries for everyone inside.
quotes: suffers a penalty to the recovery roll for those wounds equal to the aura strength

entries.title: Magical Reactions to the Infernal
entries.summary: Magic-realm beings avoid Infernal auras, and magi casting inside one may not notice the fatigue the aura costs them unless they pass a Perception roll.
quotes: Perception + Magic Theory roll against an Ease Factor of (9 + aura strength)

entries.title: Divine Reactions to the Infernal
entries.summary: Divine-affiliated characters sense the corruption of an Infernal aura more easily, and those with a Faith Score are immune to the extra effects of the specific kinds of Infernal aura.
quotes: receives a +3 bonus to all Perception rolls that would reveal the corrupt nature of the aura
characters with a Faith Score of at least 1 are immune to the additional effects imposed by different varieties of Infernal aura

entries.title: Faerie Reactions to the Infernal
entries.summary: Faeries are terrified of Infernal auras and rarely linger; their Supernatural Powers are weak and ineffectual there.
quotes: The expression of Faerie-derived Supernatural Powers is often weak and ineffectual in Infernal auras.

entries.title: Tarnished Auras
entries.summary: A tarnished aura is tied to one sinful Personality Trait that shifts the Traits of everyone inside and makes sinning in line with the tarnish a ritualised sin.
quotes: everyone within the aura suffers a modifier to Personality Traits equal to the strength of the aura

entries.title: Corrupted Auras
entries.summary: Corrupted auras are permanently tarnished auras of at least a minimum strength that add special sin-encouraging features, grouped as Debauched, Malevolent and Perfidious.

entries.title: Debauched Auras
entries.summary: Corrupted auras of self-indulgence and indolence, with example features such as Personality rolls to leave or resist returning and a ban on spending Confidence Points.
quotes: with an Ease Factor equal to (3 + aura strength)
Ease Factor equal to (6 + aura strength)

entries.title: Malevolent Auras
entries.summary: Corrupted auras of cruelty and violence whose example effects add the aura strength to damage and to botch dice on physical activities, corrupt creatures and reopen old demonic wounds.
quotes: The aura strength is added to any Damage total.
a number of additional botch dice equal to the aura strength

entries.title: Perfidious Auras
entries.summary: Corrupted auras of deceit and betrayal that make lies harder to detect, give Infernal beings a temporary Confidence Point, and punish failed Confidence-modified rolls.
quotes: all attempts to spot a lie have the aura strength added to the Ease Factor

entries.title: Mendip Battlefield: Aura
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura of the Mendip battlefield and notes that Faerie and Infernal influence is present in stories though no such aura exists yet.
quotes: The battlefield has a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: The Cave of the Inscription (aura and Watching Wards)
entries.summary: Describes the cave that binds Somerset's Winter faeries, its Magic aura, and the Watching Wards that guard the inscription and ink.
quotes: The cave has a Magic aura of 6, which rises to 8 if the second working is written on the wall.
Each spell has a Penetration of +20.

entries.title: The Nature and Effects of The Second Working
entries.summary: Explains how inscribing the second working changes the faerie nature of Somerset and how Faerie auras in the county are reduced and converted to Magic auras.
quotes: Most Faerie auras in Somerset, if lower than 10, fall by 4 points.

entries.title: Divine Auras of German Churches
entries.summary: Gives the strengths of Divine auras for the great cathedrals, other cathedrals and ordinary cities in Germany and notes where Divine auras are generally strongest and weakest.
quotes: The cathedral of Mainz, as the seat of a Holy See, has a Divine aura of 7
most cities have a Divine aura of 3

entries.title: Constantinople's Auras (layered, fluctuating realm auras)
entries.summary: Explains how Divine, Infernal, Faerie and Magic auras overlap in Constantinople, why most Divine auras are Dominion auras tied to worshipers, how auras vary with the calendar and meet at borders, and that Magic auras are no longer maintained.
quotes: Most of the Divine auras are Dominion rather than empyreal auras, meaning that their strength and size are determined by the number of faithful worshipers.
In places where auras of different realms but equal strength meet, they form a border and rest against each other.

entries.title: Auras in Egypt
entries.summary: Gives typical Dominion aura strengths for holy sites, graves, workplaces and the call to prayer, how to set Faerie auras from the strongest faerie's Might, where Magic auras come from, and Infernal auras.
quotes: Faerie auras are equal to (Might of the most powerful faerie in the area /5)

generally places of worship have a Dominion aura of 4, the cemeteries and homes of the People of the Book have an aura of 3, the places of work of monotheists have an aura of 2, and land from which the call to prayer can be heard has an aura of 1

entries.title: Faerie Creatures
entries.summary: Faeries gain Vitality when humans play out their stories, cannot truly create, change or learn without mortal aid, and are predictable if you know their story.
quotes: They are interested in having humans play out their stories, because faeries gain energy, called Vitality, when this happens.

entries.title: Faerie and Other Realms
entries.summary: Explains how Faerie relates to the Divine, Infernal and Magic realms, including who is weakened by whose aura and why faeries usually settle in places with no other supernatural presence.
quotes: Faerie powers are more compatible with Magic, in that faeries are not penalized by Magic auras, and in fact derive a small benefit from them.

entries.title: Time in Faerie Regiones
entries.summary: Explains how long characters stay in a faerie regio: willing visitors who complete the story follow the Faerieland time rules, while those who affront the principal faerie are returned at a time fitting its glamour; destroying the principal faerie does not give control of time.
quotes: use the same rules to determine the length of their stay that characters who enter Faerieland do

related.text: Chapter 2: The Faerie Realm, Leaving Faerie

entries.title: Withering Away To Dust
entries.summary: Clarifies that returning from Faerie crumbles a person to dust only when they have lived many subjective years there, not simply because years passed outside.
quotes: Characters determined to flee a Faerie court do not find that they fall away to dust when they leave

entries.title: The Three Worlds of Faerie
entries.summary: The Faerie Realm is experienced as one of three worlds (Arcadia, Elysium, Eudokia) reached by the Path of Chance, Destiny or Choice, depending on how a traveler got there.

entries.title: Getting to Faerie: Threshold Strength
entries.summary: To enter the Faerie Realm characters must accumulate Threshold points equal to a Threshold strength that depends on the local aura (modified by regiones and by Realm Interaction); examples are given for Faerie and Dominion auras.
quotes: Threshold Strength: (13 – aura modifier) x 3
must accumulate a number of Threshold points equal to the Threshold strength

entries.title: Sources of Threshold Points
entries.summary: Threshold points come from geography, time, personal change, art, Threshold faeries and faerie magic; only one attempt can be made for a given set of circumstances, and success puts characters on one of the Three Paths facing a Guardian.
quotes: Only one attempt can be made to enter Faerie for any given set of circumstances
their attempt cannot be made sooner than the next moonrise

entries.title: Example Threshold
entries.summary: Worked example of totaling Threshold points from a life change and a stream crossing against the Threshold strength of a faerie-aura hill.
quotes: so the Threshold strength is 24

entries.title: Geographical Thresholds
entries.summary: Crossing borders such as roads, crossroads, treelines or regio boundaries grants Threshold points by how significant the border is, with extra points if the travelers are lost.
quotes: add 3 Threshold points for a border crossed when the travelers truly have no idea where they are
Border is Crossed While Lost: +3

entries.title: Trods
entries.summary: A trod is a boundary with its own Faerie aura that counts as at least a Significant Threshold, leads onto the Mother Road, and links the levels of a faerie regio.
quotes: they are also always accounted to be at least a Significant Threshold

entries.title: Temporal Thresholds
entries.summary: Table of Threshold points for times such as moon phases, pagan holidays, solstices and equinoxes; Faerie auras may benefit twice from the time of year.
quotes: At these times, the border between the mundane world and Faerie becomes thinner and more easily traversed.

entries.title: Personal Thresholds
entries.summary: Characters undergoing life changes, extreme emotion, or carrying faerie Virtues and Flaws contribute Threshold points (a table lists the amounts); faerie Virtue and Flaw points do not stack, and Personality Flaws count as Traits for emotion.
quotes: Threshold points from Virtues and/or Flaws are not cumulative: choose only the highest.
consider him to have a Personality Trait of +3 (if it is a Minor Flaw) or +6 (if it is a Major Flaw)

entries.title: Artistic Endeavor (Threshold)
entries.summary: Art that evokes Faerie and is viewed or performed by the travelers adds its Aesthetic Quality to their Threshold points and hints at which world they enter.
quotes: Add the Aesthetic Quality (either Dexterity + Craft Ability or Communication + Profession Ability of the Artist

entries.title: Assistance of Threshold Faeries
entries.summary: Faeries with the Spirit Away power can add Threshold points, but cannot open the Threshold alone; many also serve as Guardian of the Threshold.
quotes: A Threshold faerie cannot attract the Threshold to the mundane realm on its own even if its Might exceeds the Threshold strength.

entries.title: The Guardian of the Threshold
entries.summary: The first entity met on entering Faerie tests the characters' resolve by offering a choice; describes passive, animal, human and monster Guardians and sets the Guardian's minimum Faerie Might.
quotes: a successful Intelligence + Faerie Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 6 will provide additional hints
All Guardians of the Threshold have a Faerie Might at least equal to the Threshold total of the group

entries.title: The Power of God in the Faerie Realm
entries.summary: Divine restrictions still bind faeries in Faerie (wards based on religious symbols), and True Faith, miracles and relics work as potently there as elsewhere.
quotes: so characters with True Faith, miraculous powers, or relics find these things just as potent as they are elsewhere

entries.title: Environment and the Faerie Aura
entries.summary: Natural rules bend to the story in Faerie, and the whole realm has a strong Faerie aura that boosts magic but adds extra botch dice, producing strange faerie botches (such as a spell becoming a faerie).
quotes: The Faerie Realm has a pervasive Faerie aura of 10, meaning that most magi receive a +5 bonus but roll an additional ten botch dice in any magical actions.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.92-96 Animae Magic

entries.title: Lands of Story and Fable
entries.summary: Each story in Faerie is its own bounded kingdom, so characters cannot travel outside the story's scope, and travel within it is driven by choices and dramatic needs; changes made in Faerie do not change the mundane world's stories.
quotes: It is impossible to travel between stories, for the kingdom is as big as the story needs it to be.

entries.title: Vitality, Fable Points and Fable Score
entries.summary: Mortals in Faerie earn fable points by playing along with its stories; points raise a fable score or can be spent for a bonus to a roll equal to the score, and everything is lost when the character leaves.
quotes: Fable Point Expenditure: +(fable score) to one roll
Increase Fable Score: fable points equal to 1 + (current fable score)
To increase one's fable score requires the expenditure of a number of fable points equal to the current score plus one.

entries.title: Gaining Fable Points
entries.summary: A character gains a one-time fable point each time he chooses to act with a faerie story rather than against it; a list of example triggers is given, with a note on how high fable scores increase time lost and Warping.
quotes: he expends vitality and gains a fable point in return
players should find it easy to earn their characters 10 or more every session in Faerie

entries.title: Becoming Faerie Through Fable (Swapping Virtues and Flaws)
entries.summary: A character's fable score lets the player swap that many Virtues (and matching Flaws) for faerie ones while in Faerie, with rules for Might pool, faerie bodies, Abilities as Pretences and learning powers as Benedictions.
quotes: A player can choose to exchange a number of his character's Virtues equal to the fable score with Virtues listed in Chapter 3: Faerie Characters; Major Virtues count as three Virtues for these purposes.
He must take one of these Virtues before he can take the Increased Might Virtue.

entries.title: Creativity in the Faerie Realm
entries.summary: Characters with unspent fable points can bargain with Faerie itself, offering a creative performance and a promise of service in exchange for changing the environment, symbolism or a faerie's attitude.

entries.title: Crafting an Offer
entries.summary: How to roll an Offer Total, what an offer costs, and the Ease Factor by threat level (set by the obstacle the change overcomes, not by the size of the change).
quotes: Offer Total: Communication + Charm or (Profession) Ability or (Craft) Ability + Offer Modifier + Promise Modifier + Change Modifier + stress die
Making an offer requires the expenditure of a fable point and a Long Term Fatigue Level

entries.title: Offer Modifiers
entries.summary: Table of bonuses to offer rolls for goods, crafts, Virtues and artistic reputation (only the highest applies), plus a penalty for changes in Elysium.
quotes: A character can only gain a single bonus from a Virtue, or for an offer of goods; use the highest bonus that applies.
offer rolls to cause changes in Elysium have a penalty of 6

entries.title: The Promise of Service
entries.summary: The offer must include a promise of action that transfers vitality; a table of Promise Modifiers rises or falls with how mundane or cunning the promised task is.
quotes: the human character must make a promise to perform some action that symbolically transfers the vitality to Faerie

entries.title: Changes in Environment
entries.summary: Using artistic Abilities to alter the glamour of the local area; a table gives Change Modifiers for altering a single object versus the whole immediate environment.
quotes: Change a single object in the environment for the characters to use as a tool to overcome the threat.

entries.title: Changes in Attitude
entries.summary: Altering a faerie's role or intentions in a scene for a single transaction and person; Change Modifiers depend on how far the faerie's apparent Personality Traits shift.
quotes: This may be expressed by changing the faerie's apparent Personality Traits by up to 3 points.

entries.title: Changes in Symbolism
entries.summary: Altering a faerie's motif through an understanding of symbolism; Change Modifiers depend on how closely the new motif relates to the old, and faeries often resent the attempt.
quotes: This may be expressed by changing the motif of the faerie to another, strongly related motif.

entries.title: Example of Using Creativity
entries.summary: Worked example in which a minstrel weighs several offers against a blizzard threat, combining Change and Promise modifiers.
quotes: A closing blizzard is a Serious threat (Ease Factor 12).

entries.title: Consequences of Creativity
entries.summary: Guidance that creativity should not be settled by a single roll, costs fable points and Fatigue, bypasses only one plot element, and should be as enjoyable as the story it replaces.
quotes: Creativity cannot entirely bypass an entire story, just a single plot element.

entries.title: The Subjective Nature of Time
entries.summary: Options for the storyguide when characters who spent different times in Faerie return together, such as using the rescuers' rate or aging the rescued person.
quotes: Time passes at the rate determined by the rescuers.

entries.title: Leaving Faerie
entries.summary: A visit ends when the story concludes and the characters meet the Guardian of the Threshold again, which has changed to reflect the story's outcome; passing it returns them to the mundane world.
quotes: passing the Guardian the second time returns the characters to the mundane world

entries.title: Warping and the Passage of Time in Faerie
entries.summary: On leaving Faerie the final fable score sets how much mortal time passes per Faerie day; a character may take Warping points to reduce the effective fable score, groups share the lowest dilation, and aging follows time in Faerie.
quotes: Every Warping point taken reduces the effective fable score by 1.
Magi do not need to check to see if they enter Twilight for receiving these Warping points.
characters in the Faerie Realm make aging rolls according to the time spent in Faerie, not the time that has passed in the real world

entries.title: Audience Participation in Faerie Stories
entries.summary: Introduces two ways to give players control in stories set in the Faerie Realm: player-driven stories, where players describe the scenery, and player-influenced stories, where players use plot devices.
quotes: allow a player to change the events that affect his character without changing the flow of the story too dramatically

entries.title: Player-Driven Stories
entries.summary: The storyguide asks players to describe the scenery they find in Arcadia, then assigns each described element its role in the story; works best the first time through.
quotes: The scene's contents are described by the players, but their role is determined by the storyguide.

entries.title: Example Plot Devices
entries.summary: A list of proverb-style plot devices that storyguides can hand to players for player-influenced stories.

entries.title: Player-Influenced Stories (Plot Devices)
entries.summary: Each player secretly receives a proverb-style plot device usable once to alter a situation affecting his own character, subject to storyguide veto; successful use earns a Confidence point reward and a fable point for the affected character.
quotes: a generic plot device that he can use once during the adventure in the Faerie Realm
Successfully employing a plot device is worth the reward of a bonus Confidence point at the end of the story, and also earns the character to whom it was applied a fable point.

entries.title: Example of Arcadian Story Creation
entries.summary: Worked example of building an Arcadian story by choosing story elements, linking them, and picking a start point.

entries.title: Pitfalls in Player-Run Stories
entries.summary: Limits on player control: the storyguide may veto input, players describe but do not assign roles, plot devices affect only one scene and the player's own character, and techniques should be varied on repeat visits.
quotes: A player-influenced device is similarly limited in that it can affect only a single scene (and only the player's own character)

entries.title: Planning Arcadian Stories
entries.summary: Procedure for building a free-form Arcadian story: choose story elements, assign each a role or act, link each to one to three others, pick a start point, and let characters move along the links.
quotes: a good guide is to take one per story experience point you intend to hand out

entries.title: Story Elements Template
entries.summary: Explains that Faerie adventures are built from Actor, Prop and Scenery story elements, each with a Path of Chance, Path of Destiny and Forking Path interpretation, and each able to take a dramatis persona role or join an act.
quotes: Any element in one of these three categories can take one of the roles described later

related.text: Chapter 7: Telling Faerie Stories, Dramatis Personae and Acts

entries.title: Ten Thousand More Story Elements
entries.summary: Two random tables of descriptors and objects that can be rolled or chosen to generate new story elements.
quotes: Choose a descriptor and an object from the following two lists; or else roll two simple dice, once for each list.

entries.title: Regiones
entries.summary: Introduces regiones, layered levels of aura at one physical location whose higher levels have stronger auras and stranger inhabitants.
quotes: Regiones consist of several levels of aura, layered one on top of another in order of increasing power, the lowest level is connected to the mundane world.

entries.title: Entering and Leaving Regiones
entries.summary: The three ways into a regio (being led, entering voluntarily by sight or path, or getting lost) and the roll and Ease Factor for seeing into a regio level.
quotes: REGIO SIGHT ROLL: Perception + Appropriate Ability + Stress Die
EASE FACTOR: 5 + (2 × difference between current level's aura and sought level's aura)

entries.title: Magic in Regiones
entries.summary: Powers used in a regio level are modified by that level's aura per the Realm Interaction Table, with doubled botch dice for powers of a different realm.
quotes: any power used within a regio of a realm different from that of the power attracts twice the normal number of botch dice.

entries.title: The Origins of Regiones
entries.summary: Two common ways regiones arise (a besieged aura moving up, or a powerful event creating a new level), and that Hermetic magi cannot create them at will.

entries.title: Traversing the Regiones (seeing across aura and regio boundaries)
entries.summary: A worked example of the roll to see into a regio of a different realm from inside another aura, and how subsuming the surrounding aura changes the Ease Factor.
quotes: Perception + Second Sight simple roll against an Ease Factor of 5 + (2 x (2 + 6)) = 21
Perception + Second Sight simple roll against an Ease Factor of 5 + (2 x (6 – 1)) = 15

entries.title: Magic Regiones
entries.summary: Explains how Magic regiones arise (mainly from aura fracturing on a botch, or from an impinging foreign aura), how new levels are generated and how Warping is handled, and what happens when levels vanish or return as the aura score changes.
quotes: A regio can never achieve more levels than the aura score plus 1, however.
all living things in it immediately drop down to the next-lower level and gain 3 Warping Points

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.53

entries.title: Faerie Regiones
entries.summary: Introduces regiones in Faerie areas, which arise from an affront or injury to the glamour of the presiding faerie.
quotes: They are caused by an affront or injury to the glamour of the presiding faerie in a regio.

entries.title: Finding a Faerie Regio Entrance
entries.summary: Faerie regio entrances are usually opened by performing a symbolic action; lists the ways to find one (Sight Virtues, invitation, learned action, Arcane Connection, True Love, Intellego Vim, Faerie Lore guess) with rolls for reading or guessing the entrance.
quotes: Perception + Awareness roll against an Ease Factor of (5 + twice the difference between the current aura and the next level)
This requires an Intelligence + Faerie Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 15.
Entrances to Faerieland from a faerie regio are treated as regio levels with an aura of 10, unless a trod runs through the regio.

related.text: ArM5 p.158 Piercing the Faerie Veil

entries.title: Faerie Roads
entries.summary: Faeries have a right of way along traditional paths, often corpse roads; travelers on them are generally left alone if they follow custom, the roads have a threshold faerie owner, and time on them flows oddly.
quotes: It is usual to pay a traditional toll for use of the road.

entries.title: Regio Levels as Acts
entries.summary: Faerie regio levels can be structured like acts of a story, each a discrete series of tests presented by progressively more potent lieutenants of the principal faerie, culminating in a final confrontation.
quotes: Each level of the regio corresponds to a discrete series of tests that the human must face.

entries.title: Divine Regiones
entries.summary: Introduces Divine regiones as holy pocket realms, how they come into being, and the two kinds, terrestrial and celestial.

entries.title: Terrestrial Regiones
entries.summary: Describes terrestrial Divine regiones, which are holy versions of a real place and typify a virtue.

entries.title: Inside Terrestrial Regiones
entries.summary: What visitors find inside a terrestrial regio, including how potent levels can yield vis from ordinary things.

entries.title: Inside Celestial Regiones (Celestial Disorientation)
entries.summary: Rolls and penalties for mortals who enter a celestial regio, and the limits on prolonged exposure that lead to Fatigue loss and Warping.
quotes: OVERCOME CELESTIAL DISORIENTATION: Stamina + Dominion Lore + stress dice
CELESTIAL DISORIENTATION EASE FACTOR: Regio Rating x3
PROLONGED EXPOSURE LIMIT: Stamina + Parma Magica (or similar Ability) + 3

entries.title: Infernal Regiones
entries.summary: Infernal regiones are places God has left to the Infernal; Divine powers are suspended or penalised there and joy is impossible. Introduces the Tartaran and Abyssal types.
quotes: Holy Powers or Holy magic suffer a penalty to their rolls equal to the aura strength of the Infernal regio

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapter 3: Blessed by God

entries.title: Abyssal Regiones
entries.summary: Regiones of privation: every Characteristic is reduced by the aura strength, and each day inside risks madness in the form of a temporary Flaw.
quotes: Every one of the eight Characteristics is reduced by a number of points equal to the strength of the aura in an Abyssal regio

entries.title: Leap of Homecoming and Regiones
entries.summary: Sidebar on how Rego Corpus teleportation effects interact with regio boundaries: usually they can cross, but some regiones cannot be entered or left this way and this cannot be reliably predicted.
quotes: some regiones cannot be entered or left via Rego Corpus effects

entries.title: Angers: Béhuard Island Dominion over Magic
entries.summary: Describes a former pagan shrine on an island in the Loire whose weak Magic aura has been overwhelmed by a Dominion aura from local prayer, and notes one nearby valley free of any Dominion aura. A worked example of Dominion displacing Magic in a populated Christian region.
quotes: their attentions have raised a Dominion aura to swamp the level-2 Magic aura of the old pagan shrine

entries.title: Tavant: Residual Magic Aura Under a Church
entries.summary: A church built over the ruins of the old covenant of Sinapis keeps a residual Magic aura that is normally overridden by the Dominion aura.
quotes: The residual Magic aura can only reassert itself when the Dominion aura is at its weakest.

entries.title: Tours: Magic and Faerie Auras Around the City
entries.summary: Lists several nearby sites with stated aura levels: a Roman tower with a Magic aura that grows stronger toward its top, a cave valley suited to a covenant site with an Aquam vis source, and a dolmen whose Faerie aura strengthens when the fae are present.
quotes: The structure normally has a Faerie aura of level 3, but this rises to 5 when the fae are present

entries.title: Gennes: Nymph Regio
entries.summary: A small Magic regio beside a Roman amphitheatre where nymphs may give Aquam vis to visitors who please them, and where male visitors may find it hard to leave.
quotes: There is a small Magic regio close beside this, where several nymphs live in a Gallo-Roman shrine.

entries.title: Noirmoutier: Island Magic Aura with Higher Beach
entries.summary: A coastal island with a modest Magic aura and a sacred beach where the aura is stronger, described as a possible covenant site with notable resources.
quotes: The isle has a Magic aura of level 3.

entries.title: Poitiers: Dominion Auras of Holy Sites
entries.summary: Gives Dominion aura levels for specific holy sites, including one that has faded over time through changed usage.
quotes: the Dominion aura there has faded to level 4
it has a Dominion aura of 5

entries.title: Vézère Valley: Magic Aura, Aligned Caves and Regio
entries.summary: Describes an extensive Magic aura under a river valley whose cave paintings and formations give higher, Form-aligned aura levels, plus a two-level regio reached through linked caves.
quotes: Places with the most vivid depictions have a Magic aura of 5 or 6, aligned with Animal

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.25

entries.title: Clermont: Moon-Gated Regio
entries.summary: A regio grove with a Terram vis spring beneath a city, entered through a spring-fed clump of trees and passable only at a particular phase of the moon.
quotes: The way in and out is only accessible when the moon is full.

entries.title: Auvergne Mountains: Puy de Dôme Regio and Healing Springs
entries.summary: Covers a regio on the Puy de Dôme entered by following the Roman road, scattered low Magic auras that yield vis in particular ways, and hot springs and gases that give a bonus to recovery rolls when used for a limited time.
quotes: Treat half an hour spent immersed in the water or breathing in the gas as giving a +3 to the recovery roll

entries.title: Fontainebleau: Fountain of Fair Waters Faerie Regio
entries.summary: A Faerie regio around a spring with a nymph, tolerant of humble visitors but cursing hunters who persist, with transformed boulders that can be harvested for vis.
quotes: It has a Faerie aura of 6.

entries.title: Bavacum: Seven Roads and Mercury's Shortcuts
entries.summary: A Magic aura site where one of seven Roman roads gives a shortened journey depending on the heavens, with a roll to predict which road is active and an annual day when all roads work and footprints yield vis.
quotes: An Intelligence + Artes Liberales roll against an Ease Factor of 12 may be made to accurately predict which road will be active at any given time.

entries.title: Faux de Verzy: Faerie Aura Grove
entries.summary: A feared grove of twisted beeches with a stated Faerie aura, where captives are said to return scarred.
quotes: This place, which has a Faerie aura of 4, is shunned by the nearby peasants.

entries.title: Nanteuil: Possible Divine Regio
entries.summary: A Templar priory in a remote vale that one magus recorded as a regio of possibly Divine origin, though others blame a Twilight episode.
quotes: found it to be a regio, possibly of Divine origin

entries.title: Blue Springs of the Somme: Faerie Pools
entries.summary: Enchanted pools with Faerie auras of varying strength whose sprites steal things or reward gifts and bless infants.
quotes: The pools have Faerie auras of differing strengths, up to 3.

entries.title: Caves of Naours: Pact with a Genius Loci
entries.summary: An underground village protected by a mutual-protection pact with a cave spirit, set within a weak Magic aura.
quotes: A Magic aura of 2 pervades throughout.

entries.title: Clairvaux: Divine Aura of an Abbey
entries.summary: Gives the Divine aura of a major Cistercian abbey as an example of a strong Dominion site.
quotes: The entire abbey has a Divine aura of 6.

entries.title: Catalaunian Fields: Infernal Aura and Solstice Regio
entries.summary: A battlefield with a Malevolent Infernal aura that on one night of the year opens into an Infernal regio of fighting shades, where Perdo and Corpus vis can be harvested, some of it Infernally tainted.
quotes: A Malevolent Infernal aura of 3

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.15

entries.title: Mont Auxois: Magic and Divine Aura on One Hill
entries.summary: A haunted hilltop ruin that keeps a Magic aura and could suit a covenant, with a separate Divine aura around a martyr's healing fountain on one edge.
quotes: The place retains a Magic aura and might make a suitable site for a covenant
On the southwestern edge of the hilltop, a Divine aura prevails.

entries.title: Cave of Sabinus: Genius Loci and Luctatio
entries.summary: A cave with a demanding genius loci that permits Aquam vis to be harvested from its spring, treated by the Tribunal as a contested vis site (a luctatio).
quotes: the site is, however, considered a luctatio by the Tribunal

entries.title: Cluny: Optional Infernal Corruption Inside a Divine Aura
entries.summary: Offers an optional dark option for a saga in which Infernal auras hide within, or weaken, the strong Divine aura of a wealthy monastery.
quotes: as an optional, somewhat dark take for your saga

entries.title: What is Magic?
entries.summary: Explains that magical things are idealized versions of mundane things and sets out three guiding facts about Magic (objective, ancient, mysterious) to help players and storyguides decide how magical power shows up.
quotes: Magic is objective.
Magic is ancient.
Magic is mysterious.

entries.title: Rules of the Realm
entries.summary: General rules for characters inside the Magic Realm: no experience is gained but vis accrues instead, no Aging rolls are made, spell durations are stretched, Arcane Connections behave differently, and the whole Realm has a Magic aura.
quotes: The entire Magic Realm has a Magic aura of 10.
characters do not receive experience points while they are in the Magic Realm

entries.title: Into the Magic Realm
entries.summary: Introduces the three ways to cross from the mundane realm into the Magic Realm: regiones, magic powers and magical disasters.

entries.title: Entering via Magic Regiones
entries.summary: Describes crossing a Magic regio boundary or stepping past the exterior of a high-level regio as a way into the Magic Realm.

entries.title: Entering via Magic Powers
entries.summary: Characters with a Magic Might Score can pass into the Magic Realm through objects connected to the same Form as their Might, and can lead others with them; magic creatures may have powers for this.

entries.title: Entering via Magical Disasters
entries.summary: A magical disaster can throw the wielder or surroundings into the Magic Realm; affected characters try to avoid it with a Twilight Avoidance roll using the disaster's botches.
quotes: substituting the number of botches on the disaster roll for the number of Warping Points gained

entries.title: Boundaries and Vestiges
entries.summary: Rules for realm boundaries (a level that adds to magical activities, doubles for the aligned Form, adds botch dice and produces vis each season) and for vestiges, which are insubstantial Form-aligned images with their own connection level.
quotes: Realm boundaries have a level that ranges from 0 to 10, like regiones, and this is added as a bonus to all magic activities within the area
add a number of botch dice equal to the level of the boundary to every roll that benefits from the Magic aura
A number of pawns equal to (the modified level of the aura divided by 10, rounded up) appear somewhere within the boundary every season

entries.title: Magical Travel
entries.summary: How a character with Magic Might or similar powers passes through a boundary or vestige, including the travel rolls, the Familiarity modifier table, the Speed Level journey-length table, attempts to hasten the journey, botches, and how durations and Arcane Connections are affected in the Void.
quotes: Boundary Travel: stress die + Perception + appropriate Ability + Form bonus vs. ((10 – current realm boundary level) x 3) – Familiarity modifier
Vestige Travel: stress die + Perception + appropriate Ability + Form bonus vs. ((10 –level of the vestige) x 3) – Familiarity modifier
Twilight Void Travel: stress die + Stamina + Concentration + Form bonus

entries.title: The Twilight Void
entries.summary: Describes the Void's provinces (one per Form), what travelers can perceive and do there, that travelers need no food, do not age and gain neither experience nor vis, and the Twilight Comprehension roll for exploring it with its positive and negative outcomes.
quotes: Twilight Comprehension: Intelligence + Enigmatic Wisdom + stress die vs. Warping Score or (Might Score / 5) + stress die

entries.title: Advancement in the Magic Realm
entries.summary: Characters can spend the vis they collect in the Magic Realm to gain or transform Virtues and Flaws before returning, according to a table of vis costs, with limits on one transformation per season and on which Virtues qualify.
quotes: Characters do not experience more than one transformation in a single season

entries.title: Positive and Negative Traits
entries.summary: Suggestions, by Void province, for the Twilight Scars and Essential Traits a character might gain from comprehending or failing to comprehend an experience in the Twilight Void.

entries.title: Elysium and Elysian Quests
entries.summary: Elysium holds the told stories of legend; characters can enact a suitable story to gain a boon such as an insight, but the aid is indirect, Faerie in nature, and can reveal only what the tellers of the legend knew.
quotes: it is not possible to uncover secrets unknown to the tellers of the legend
The aid provided by the successful conclusion of an Elysian quest is rarely direct, and it cannot be of a non-Faerie nature.

entries.title: The Road of Destiny (Reaching Elysium)
entries.summary: Reaching Elysium requires aligning all Threshold sources toward the target story; sources inappropriate to the story subtract from the Threshold total instead of adding.
quotes: all sources of Threshold points that are inappropriate actually subtract from the total, rather than adding to it

entries.title: Identification as the Hero
entries.summary: To enact an Elysian story a character declares himself the hero after passing the Guardian, at the cost of a Confidence point, gaining a first fable point; several characters can share the role using a token.
quotes: Identification with the hero in this manner costs the character a Confidence point
Simply identifying with the hero grants the character his first fable point, and thus a fable score of 1
Each must identify himself as the hero upon entering Elysium through a firm statement and the expenditure of a Confidence point.

entries.title: Hermetic Legends in Elysium
entries.summary: Order of Hermes stories can be witnessed in Elysium but cannot reveal secrets unknown to the tellers, and conflicting versions of an event are equally true there.
quotes: witnessing and participating in such stories cannot reveal secrets

entries.title: Elysian Stories
entries.summary: Describes how Elysian stories differ from ordinary ones: the characters know the plot and success is measured by how closely they follow the legendary hero's steps; the journey needs careful planning.
quotes: The success of such an adventure is counted by the measure to which the characters have managed to walk the same steps as the legendary hero who is their role model.

entries.title: Example of Elysian Story Creation
entries.summary: Worked example breaking the story of Reynard the Fox into scenes with challenges for the characters.

entries.title: Planning Elysian Stories
entries.summary: Procedure for turning a legend into scenes: players choose the tale, the storyguide splits it into acts and defines success and obstacles for each, with complications that must not interfere with the original tale.
quotes: one element per story experience point you intend to hand out at the culmination of the quest is a good guide

entries.title: Adding New Scenes
entries.summary: When a story is too short or lacks background, the storyguide can add scenes that connect to existing acts, like a director's cut.

entries.title: Running Elysian Stories
entries.summary: Each story element must be resolved in the manner of the underlying tale; if characters derail it they must bring it back on track, and actions that do so generate fable points.
quotes: The characters are also more likely to succeed in bringing their story back on track if their actions to rectify it generate fable points

entries.title: A Twist to the Tale
entries.summary: Optional variant in which the characters take a role other than the hero, usually the villain or princess, and must steer events to the legend's outcome.
quotes: For most stories, the only appropriate dramatis personae other than the hero are the roles of villain and princess

entries.title: The Measure of Success in Elysium
entries.summary: The storyguide scores how faithfully each element was resolved; the hero's total fable points earned (all points, not only converted ones) map to a table of success levels that decide how much of the quest object is gained, including bonuses to an Initiation Script.
quotes: This score simply translates into the total number of fable points earned by the Hero while pursuing the quest.
Count all points earned, not just those converted into a fable score

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults, Initiation Scripts

entries.title: The Forking Path (Reaching Eudokia)
entries.summary: Characters on the verge of a major life change who stray into a Faerie aura typically take the Forked Path into Eudokia, usually alone or with others undergoing the same change.

entries.title: Eudokian Stories
entries.summary: Eudokian stories are mediated by a Threshold faerie governing the character's transition and focus on one or a few characters; companions may help but usually only the focal character benefits beyond Story Experience.
quotes: anyone present when the Threshold arrives is taken into Faerie at the same time

entries.title: Planning Eudokian Stories
entries.summary: Procedure for building a Eudokian story: choose a theme that determines the reward, build story elements that each present a dilemma with one choice matching the theme, and send the characters home once over half of their decisions are right.
quotes: typically one per Story Experience point you intend to hand out
is to make over half of the right decisions

entries.title: Example Story Themes, and Virtues & Flaws
entries.summary: Sidebar listing sample Eudokian themes with a situation and the Virtue and Flaw that might be awarded.

entries.title: Leaving Eudokia
entries.summary: After the challenges the mediating Threshold faerie normally reappears and sends the characters home with its Spirit Away power, possibly in a disguised form.
quotes: send them back to the mortal realm with its Spirit Away power

entries.title: Faerie Boons (Eudokia Rewards)
entries.summary: Tally correct and incorrect choices on a Eudokian journey; more correct choices give a Virtue balanced by a Charm Flaw, more incorrect ones give a temporary Flaw, with Major or Minor depending on whether all choices went one way, and a Personality Trait shifts by one point.
quotes: If the character made more correct choices than incorrect choices, then he acquires a Virtue.
If all the choices he made were correct, then the Virtue is Major, else it is Minor.
the character bears the Flaw for an amount of time equal to the time that passed while the character was in Faerie

entries.title: Example of Eudokian Story Creation
entries.summary: Worked example of assembling a Eudokian story with the theme of Resolve from five story elements.

entries.title: Magic and Sin (Saga Decision)
entries.summary: The core rules leave open whether magic is inherently sinful. This sidebar explains how each choice changes the relationship between magi, the Church, saints and angels, and what counts as penance.
quotes: If magic is inherently sinful, casting a spell is sinful no matter what the purpose.

entries.title: Who Has the Dominion?
entries.summary: Explains which groups of worshippers are protected by a Dominion, regardless of creed, and notes that heresy may cause schism.

entries.title: Dominion Power
entries.summary: Rules of thumb for how strong the Dominion is and how far it extends from a place of worship, in a church, a city and the surrounding land.
quotes: the Dominion is typically strongest where people gather to worship in a consecrated place (aura 4)

entries.title: Dominion Power Examples
entries.summary: A quick table of Dominion aura ratings by kind of area, with adjustments for night and holy days.
quotes: At night, subtract one from the rating, and add one on holy days (Sundays for example).

entries.title: Holy of Holies (the Eucharist)
entries.summary: Describes the Dominion radiated by the consecrated Eucharist in Christian churches, how it fades with distance, and what destroys it.
quotes: The Eucharist radiates a Dominion (not Empyreal aura) of five until the next Good Friday; this aura decreases by one every five paces

entries.title: Creating a Dominion Aura
entries.summary: Procedure for founding a Dominion: a celebrant, a consecrated site and a congregation, two successful Dominion rites, and then how the aura grows, fades and exceeds the usual maximum.
quotes: DOMINION RITE: Communication + Theology (or Dominion Lore) + stress die vs. Ease Factor 6
Dominion ratings higher than five are achieved through extremely holy objects, or the relics of particularly exemplary saints

entries.title: Holy Influence
entries.summary: How holy characters with spiritual authority inspire temporary Personality Traits in followers, by personal influence over a season or by a short ceremony, with a roll that sets the strength of the trait.
quotes: HOLY INFLUENCE: simple die + Presence + Leadership

entries.title: Tempers
entries.summary: Rules for holy characters invoking a temper in a Dominion aura, giving bonuses or penalties to compatible or opposed actions, with descriptions of the seven tempers.
quotes: TEMPERING AN AURA: stress die + Presence + Leadership

entries.title: Personality Traits (tempers, virtues and vices)
entries.summary: A table linking each temper to related positive Personality Traits, the vice it opposes and the negative traits, with advice on noting a trait's temper.

entries.title: Schism
entries.summary: Explains how rival holy leaders invoking different tempers in the same aura can cancel each other out, which is called schism.

entries.title: The Powers of Relics
entries.summary: Common powers every relic has: a Faith score, a Divine Might derived from it, and an aura that harms Infernal creatures, plus how specific powers work and when they fail.
quotes: A relic's Divine Might is equal to the relic's Faith score (or highest Faith score, if more than one applies) multiplied by 10, and is refreshed with every sunrise.

entries.title: Invoking a Saint
entries.summary: Any Christian may once a day ask a saint for a miracle by rolling Communication + Charm against a hidden Ease Factor; success means the saint uses one of his powers, failure allows another try the next day.
quotes: Once a day you may ask a saint for aid, hoping the saint will respond with a miracle.
INVOKING A SAINT: Communication + Charm + modifiers + a simple die vs. 15 + a simple die

entries.title: Invocation Modifiers
entries.summary: Table of situational modifiers to the roll to invoke a saint, such as being at the tomb, the feast day, donations, True Faith, recent miracles and invoking a non-patron saint.
quotes: | Invoking a saint other than a patron saint | –15 |

entries.title: Saints' Miracles
entries.summary: Saints' miracles are represented as powers with Might point costs; greater saints know most of them and lesser saints only the cheapest.
quotes: Greater saints have most of the powers, area saints have many of the powers, and lesser saints have only the lowest-costing powers.

entries.title: Growth of Towns and the Spreading Dominion
entries.summary: Describes how expanding cities convert surrounding wild land into farmland that falls under the Dominion, impairing magic and corroding vis-harvesting sites.
quotes: Each city transforms the land around itself for a distance of twenty miles, gradually converting wild spaces into farmland.
Farmland is usually covered by the Dominion, which impairs magical practice and corrodes vis-harvesting sites.

entries.title: Byzantine Saints: invoking a saint and common powers
entries.summary: Describes the Orthodox veneration of saints, the roll for invoking a saint's intercession, and a set of powers commonly used by Greek saints.
quotes: Communication + Charm + modifier + simple die vs. 15 + simple die
The petitioner does not need to eat or sleep for a number of days equal to the saint's Divine Might

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, pages 87-88

entries.title: Tainted Vis
entries.summary: Vis from Faerie, Divine and Infernal auras may be tainted, with Infernal vis adding botch dice to spellcasting and demanding an experimental-results roll for enchanted items.
quotes: At the very least, using Infernally tainted vis adds twice as many botch dice as usual to spellcasting

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, pp.18-19

versions.title: Tainted Vis (Simplified)
versions.summary: A simple fallback for troupes not using the full Infernal rules: tainted vis gives a larger casting bonus, adds botch dice for users not aligned with the Infernal, and slowly implants a sinful Personality trait in whoever carries it.
quotes: Adds 5 instead of 2 to casting totals.
Adds three botch dice per pawn, for non-Infernally aligned users.
related: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.18-19

entries.title: Faerie Vis
entries.summary: Faerie vis comes in several types that magi do not usually distinguish, though any simple Intellego Vim spell will reveal that vis is of faerie type.
quotes: with any simple Intellego Vim spell

related.text: ArM5 Sense the Nature of Vis

entries.title: Encased Vis
entries.summary: The most common faerie-area vis: Magic vis that a faerie has claimed with glamour, which faeries use as food, to make glamorous things real, and to ease role changes, while hiding the source from humans.
quotes: Encased vis is simply Magic vis that a faerie has laid glamour over, to claim possession of it.

entries.title: Anchor Vis
entries.summary: The mundane object holding a faerie's glamour is vis that magi prize when the faerie's body is destroyed; the trapped faerie stays conscious but cannot use powers, and a broken taboo on the anchor turns it into accrued vis.
quotes: A faerie remains conscious, and in its current role, while trapped in its anchor.
Anchors whose faeries break taboo become accrued vis.

entries.title: Accrued Vis
entries.summary: Vis that builds up from glamour left by faeries who end their roles, including the bodies and accoutrements shed by narrowly cognizant faeries, which may retain Pretenses a human can use.
quotes: Accrued vis forms when faeries end their roles.

entries.title: Sleeping Vis
entries.summary: Vis holding a simple glamour with no vitality, which may awaken into a faerie if given vitality; Merinita magi pay well for it.
quotes: If provided with vitality, some sleeping vis ceases to be dormant and becomes a faerie.

entries.title: Abstract Vis
entries.summary: A faerie-made counterfeit that is detected as enchanted but holds no real vis; the creator's servants must honor it, and magi cannot use it for concrete purposes such as making magic items.
quotes: Magi cannot employ abstract vis for concrete uses like crafting magic items.

entries.title: Infernal Vis
entries.summary: Introduces Infernally tainted vis, which looks ordinary to Hermetic detection but endangers non-Infernal users, and the temporary Personality Trait imposed by prolonged contact with it.
quotes: The imposed trait either starts at a score of +1, or increases the trait by 1 if the magus already possesses it.

related.text: Chapter 4: The Infernal Legions, Common Powers

entries.title: Vis Infesta
entries.summary: The mildest Infernal vis: it adds no extra botch dice beyond raw vis but makes any botch more severe, and experimentation in enchantments always yields the worst result.
quotes: one extra botch die per pawn of vis

entries.title: Vis Sordida
entries.summary: Potent but dangerous Infernal vis that boosts casting totals and Source Quality at the cost of extra botch dice, and corrupts levels of effects in items prepared with it. Includes a worked enchanting example.
quotes: Each pawn of vis sordida used to enhance a casting total adds five to the roll, rather than the +2 of standard vis.
Using vis sordida always incurs three extra botch dice per pawn used
ten levels of effects in the item are corrupted for every pawn of vis sordida used

entries.title: Vis Prava
entries.summary: The vilest Infernal vis: any roll using it is automatically a zero with extra botch dice, studying from it causes Warping, and enchanting with it ruins the item; it is far better for Infernally aligned wizards.
quotes: rolling two extra botch dice for every pawn of vis prava used
vis prava offers a +5 bonus to Casting Totals per pawn employed

entries.title: Miracles
entries.summary: How often and in what forms miracles occur in Mythic Europe (healing, punishment, miscellaneous), what makes one more likely, and how a storyguide can tune their frequency to set how Mythic the setting is.
quotes: a miracle is more likely to be granted if it is sincerely requested by a pious person, if the cause of the affliction was entirely innocent, and if an appropriate saint adds his prayers
The frequency described in the main text is a default level

versions.title: Miracles (overview)
versions.summary: Introduces the optional miracle rules: miracles come directly from God, cannot be overcome by magic or other powers, and differ from saints' miracles and from learned holy powers.
quotes: The following mechanics for miracles are optional.

entries.title: Vigils & Fasting
entries.summary: Rules for spending a night in prayer (a Confidence Point at the cost of a Fatigue level) and for fasting for a season (a Petitioning bonus at the cost of constant Fatigue).
quotes: A Fatigue level is lost, and will not be recovered until the character has made up a full night's sleep, but the character gains one Confidence Point that may be spent the next day on a specified virtuous task.
A fast lasts for a season and grants a +1 noncumulative bonus to Petitioning a Saint

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Petitioning a Saint

entries.title: Patron Saints
entries.summary: Explains who counts as a character's patron saint for invocation, and that anyone may invoke Mary or a saint whose traditional interest fits the matter at hand, with no Piety required.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Patron saints

entries.title: Faith Points
entries.summary: Faith Points are spent like Confidence Points for a bonus to a roll, normally one per roll; they do not regenerate on their own unless the character has True Faith.
quotes: Faith Points may be spent like Confidence Points to gain a +3 bonus to a roll, and usually a character may only spend 1 Faith Point on each roll.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.56-60 Faith Points

entries.title: Invocation of the Civic Patron
entries.summary: Notes that a character may ask a city's patron saint for a miracle allowing virtuous magic to ignore Dominion penalties for a scene or story.
quotes: the penalties the character suffers due to the Realm Interaction Chart are reduced to zero

entries.title: Invoking God's Aid
entries.summary: Any character who can spend Confidence or a Faith Point may pray for divine help in an endeavor, with a roll and botch rule for presumption.
quotes: INVOKING GOD'S AID: stress die + Communication + Dominion Lore

entries.title: Divine Aid Bonus Table
entries.summary: Converts the invocation total into a bonus to rolls in the scene, and describes how long it lasts and how group invocations work.
quotes: the bonus will cease to operate as soon as the player fails a roll or at the end of the scene

entries.title: Invoking God's Aid in Warfare
entries.summary: Limits on invoking God's aid in military conflict and how it combines with a Trained Group's combat bonus.
quotes: only the highest Divine Aid Bonus applies to the group's combat bonus

entries.title: Gaining Faith Points
entries.summary: Any character can acquire Faith Points through devout acts such as pilgrimage, sacraments, tests of faith or particularly pious activities.

entries.title: Infernal Creatures
entries.summary: Infernal creatures may take attractive forms, and their lies cannot be detected by Magic realm powers, though ordinary investigation can still reveal the truth.
quotes: The lies of creatures that belong to the Infernal realm cannot be detected by the powers of the Magic realm.

entries.title: Heresy and Corruption
entries.summary: Guidance for storyguides on when heresy actually counts as Infernal rather than merely mistaken: most heretics are sincere believers, and a false teaching is Infernal only when it leads to real sinful acts.
quotes: A wrong teaching only becomes Infernal when it leads people directly to sinful behavior, and hence to damnation.

entries.title: What Counts as Sin
entries.summary: Explains how the storyguide judges whether an act is sinful: aiding the Infernal always is, while other acts depend on whether they are selfish or secret.

entries.title: Types of Sin
entries.summary: Distinguishes mortal sins from venial sins and notes that compelled or inadvertent acts are not sins, but dealing with the Infernal always stains the soul.

entries.title: Sinful Traits
entries.summary: Optional method of tying each Personality Trait to a virtue or vice, with a table of the seven deadly sins and their related traits, so that sin-related rolls can be called for by category.
quotes: When dealing with opposing traits, treat the trait's value as negative.

entries.title: Redemption
entries.summary: Notes that any sinner, however corrupt, may escape Hell by truly repenting, with the means of absolution depending on faith.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapters 4, 5, 6

entries.title: Gaining Confidence through Sin
entries.summary: Characters with a sinful Personality Trait can earn Confidence Points by indulging in that sin for a season or through a ritualised act that also costs a Warping Point; even characters without Confidence can bank and spend the points.
quotes: Either activity yields a Confidence Point upon completion.
Generally speaking, venial sins are sufficient for traits of +3 or less

entries.title: Profaning the Holy
entries.summary: Rules for turning a holy object or relic into a pawn of Infernal vis by spending Confidence or overcoming Faith, with example uses such as the Host.
quotes: To profane a holy object costs the character a point of Confidence.
the character profaning it must have a Confidence Score greater than the relic's Faith Score to succeed

entries.title: Divine Warping (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces Divine Warping, the Dominion-flavoured form of Warping, and the Divine Ascent peculiar to holy mystics.

entries.title: Causes of Divine Warping
entries.summary: Divine Warping comes from Divine auras, powerful Divine effects and Divine botches; it uses normal Warping mechanics with different flavour, and those with Faith Points or holy powers avoid aura Warping.
quotes: There is no mechanical difference between types of Warping.

entries.title: Divine Auras and Warping
entries.summary: Strong Divine auras in large churches are a common source of Divine Warping, though many residents are protected by Faith Points or abilities.

entries.title: Miracles and Warping
entries.summary: Witnessing a sufficiently high-level miracle gives a Warping Point, except for those it was meant to benefit.
quotes: A character in the presence of a miracle whose level is thirty or greater gains one Warping Point.

entries.title: Divine and Holy Powers and Warping
entries.summary: Powers of Divine beings and holy powers also cause Warping once their level is high enough.
quotes: will also cause Warping if the level of the power is thirty or higher

entries.title: Infernal Warping
entries.summary: Describes how Warping dominated by sin or Infernal contact produces sin-encouraging Flaws and Infernal Virtues at successive Warping Scores.
quotes: The character acquires a Minor Personality Flaw that reflects his obsession with sinful behavior.

entries.title: Causes of Infernal Warping
entries.summary: Lists the ways a character gains Infernal Warping Points: ritualised sin, Infernal auras and regiones, Infernal Powers, and botches with unholy abilities.
quotes: every time a character ritualizes a sin to acquire Confidence Points, she gains a Warping Point
if the level of the Power is 30 or more, or if a demon spends 6 or more points of Might activating the power
One Warping Point is gained for each zero on a botch dice when using an unholy Power or Infernal Supernatural Ability.

entries.title: Hermetic Magic and the Sacraments
entries.summary: Describes the supernatural effects of the sacraments that magi can observe, such as baptismal names not serving as Sympathetic Connections and bodies that have received Extreme Unction being immune to magic for a few days.
quotes: a baptismal name cannot be used as a Sympathetic Connection to aid Penetration (unlike a birth name)
bodies that have received Extreme Unction cannot be affected by magic for three days

entries.title: The Practice of Confession
entries.summary: How confession and penance work for Christian characters, including the temporary Confidence point and holy connection until penance is done, with notes on how confession differs in Judaism and Islam and on secular confession.
quotes: The character gains a temporary Confidence point that can be used to help him complete his penance

entries.title: Possession and Exorcism
entries.summary: An exorcist spends a Confidence or Faith Point and generates an Exorcism Total, which succeeds if it meets an Ease Factor equal to the Might Points the demon has invested in the possessed victim; ordination as exorcist, holy water and a crucifix add bonuses.
quotes: Exorcism Total: Stress Die + Bonuses
If the Exorcism Total equals or exceeds an Ease Factor equal to the number of Might Points invested in the energumen by the demon, then the demon is exorcised.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.32 Possession

entries.title: The Sacraments
entries.summary: Treats the seven Sacraments as supernatural Divine powers that need no Penetration but require willing participants, with a Faith Point available from each and specific effects for baptism, confirmation, Mass, marriage, penance, ordination and extreme unction.
quotes: A character may not have more than 1 Faith Point from each Sacrament.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.74 Sacraments

versions.title: The Sacraments
versions.summary: Sacraments are holy ceremonies with automatic supernatural effects on willing participants, most granting a Faith Point (at most one per sacrament) and some other benefits, covering baptism, confirmation, marriage, penance, the Eucharist, ordination and extreme unction, plus excommunication and interdict.
quotes: Sacraments only affect willing participants, and for this reason they do not have effect levels.
A character may have no more than one Faith Point from a given sacrament
