entries.title: Religious Rites for New Babies
entries.summary: Christian baptism and the equivalent Jewish and Muslim birth rites cancel non-Divine supernatural effects on a child and drive out possessing spirits, without hindering The Gift.
quotes: baptism cancels any supernatural effect not associated with the Divine realm that may be affecting the child at the time of baptism

entries.title: Studying from Exhibits (realia)
entries.summary: Restates the realia study rules: a realia is a study source that can be used a number of times equal to its Source Quality, and Source Quality drops when several characters study from the same exhibit at once.
quotes: The number of times that a character may study from a particular realia is equal to its Source Quality.
up to four characters studying reduce the Source Quality by 2; up to eight characters reduce the Source Quality by 3

entries.title: Exhibit Source Quality
entries.summary: Sidebar giving guideline Source Quality bands for exhibits depending on how many items they hold.
quotes: Unparalleled: Source Quality 11+
Comprehensive: Source Quality 8-10
Cursory: Source Quality 5-7

entries.title: Competition for Exhibit Study Access
entries.summary: Access rules for Tablinum's open exhibits and a stress die roll to see how many other characters also want to study from the same exhibit in a season.
quotes: roll a stress die against an Ease Factor of 3

entries.title: Realms: Belonging and Affiliation
entries.summary: Introduces the four realms and the difference between a creature belonging to a realm and merely being affiliated with it.
quotes: A creature that belongs to a realm cannot be affiliated with any other realm.

entries.title: Creatures of a Realm
entries.summary: Guidance on how a creature's realm shapes its attitude towards humans (Infernal, Magic, Divine, Faerie), illustrated with a talking dog in each realm.
quotes: Creatures of the Infernal are always interested in corrupting and harming human beings

entries.title: Realm Affiliations (Infernal Virtues and Abilities)
entries.summary: A table of the Supernatural Virtues, Flaws and Abilities in this book with the realm each is affiliated to for realm interaction, and notes on aura penalties and re-flavouring Powers for other realms.
quotes: | Ablating | Infernal | Chapter 11 |

entries.title: Lacunae
entries.summary: Explains lacunae, small patches inside a city where the Dominion does not dominate, so magi can cast there without Dominion realm interaction penalties. Describes their typical size, aura and the theories of how they form.
quotes: Lacunae allow magi to cast spells without realm interaction penalties due to the Dominion, provided they do not target things within the Dominion.

entries.title: Finding New Lacunae
entries.summary: Gives the ways lacunae enter a saga (covenant creation, character creation, story rewards) and the seasonal Area Lore search for them, including how many a character knows and the need for a limitation on bonus lacunae.
quotes: A character seeking lacunae spends a season, then rolls Intelligence + Area Lore against an Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: Ecclesiastical Lords and Town Divine Aura
entries.summary: Describes how bishops and abbots grant charters and gives the Divine aura level of a town under an ecclesiastical charter, noting that ecclesiastics usually cannot become citizens.
quotes: Towns with ecclesiastical charters have a Divine aura of 3 within the town-walls

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.10

entries.title: Supernatural Charter Lords (Faerie and Demonic Charters)
entries.summary: Covers towns chartered by faerie lords or by demons: the effect on the town's Divine aura, and the typical Infernal Might and services a charter demon offers townsfolk, with their modifiers.
quotes: have a reduced Divine aura of 1 within the townwalls
A typical charter demon has an Infernal Might of 15 (Mentem)
Relief from disease: +2 Living Condition Modifier.

entries.title: Birth Apparitions
entries.summary: Characters with realm-linked Virtues or Flaws may be born with a brief apparition from their realm, whose Might depends on how strong the Virtue or Flaw is; an Aegis of the Hearth may block it.
quotes: Most have a Might Score of 5, if the child has a Minor Supernatural Virtue or Flaw, or 10 for a Major Virtue or Flaw, and rarely have magical powers.

entries.title: St. Broch's Fountain Blessing (Lamballe and St. Brieuc)
entries.summary: A once-a-week devotional ritual at St. Broch's fountain after Sunday Mass that grants a temporary one-step shift to a Personality Trait, up to the usual cap, lasting until sunset.
quotes: a character may dip his right hand into the fountain and devoutly make the sign of the cross to gain a Blessing that gives a temporary change to a Personality Trait by one step
The blessing lasts until sunset.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.51

entries.title: Reading Hieroglyphs and Tomb Warnings
entries.summary: Explains the medieval belief that learned Copts can read hieroglyphs, and gives a stress roll with Ease Factors for grasping the gist of tomb warnings and curses as taught by the Seekers' Guild.
quotes: the gist of a text can be understood with an Intelligence + Profession: Seeker stress roll against an Ease Factor related to the age and complexity of the text (common curses are Ease Factor 6, typical texts are Ease Factor 9)

entries.title: False Powers
entries.summary: Explains Powers aligned with the Magic or Faerie realms that are subtly tainted by the Infernal, how Divine investigation perceives them, and how Powers become False through Warping, botches or infernal interference.
quotes: False Powers are no different from any other Supernatural Virtues or Flaws, save that Divine Powers (and some Infernal ones) perceive them as unholy

entries.title: Supernatural Interests in Adolescents
entries.summary: Describes how Infernal, Divine, Faerie and Magic beings treat adolescents, including a bonus for adolescents invoking a patron saint and the point that magical compulsion toward sin is not itself a sin.
quotes: who receive a +1 bonus to the roll to invoke their patron saint

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87

entries.title: Creating Divine Regiones
entries.requires: Divine creature with sufficient Divine Might
entries.summary: Rules for divine beings with enough Divine Might creating temporary Divine regiones, and the Might cost of sustaining them.
quotes: Divine beings with a Divine Might score of 20 or greater have the ability to create temporary Divine regiones of either kind.
The creature must spend at least 10 Divine Might points, which creates a single-level regio with a rating of 1.

entries.title: Spontaneous Regiones
entries.requires: A miracle, holy power or expenditure of Divine Might
entries.summary: Notes that powerful divine acts may create a temporary Divine regio, with no precise system beyond story needs.

entries.title: The City of Luz (Celestial Regio)
entries.summary: A Divine regio where those inside do not die; it explains how to summon a pathway to it, how recovery rolls and aging behave inside, and the penalty for leaving after a long stay.
quotes: It takes a Purity (or Merkavah) + Intervention miraculous effect of base 35 to summon a pathway to the city gates
any rolls of 0 or less impose an Aging Point in any physical Characteristic

entries.title: Bear Island: Chytus Harbor (Gegenees external vis boulders)
entries.summary: A Faerie aura site where the Gegenees keep their external vis in boulders; the number of vis-holding boulders is scaled to the saga's power level and moving or threatening them provokes an assault.
quotes: How many of these hold vis depends on how many Gegenees you need for your saga: 50 for a low powered saga, 200 for a medium powered saga, and 1,000 or more for a high powered saga.

entries.title: Bear Island: Temenos of Dindyméné (dual Magic and Faerie aura)
entries.summary: A sacred grove holding overlapping Magic and Faerie auras, where the older Magic aura normally suppresses the Faerie one except on certain anniversaries and festival dates, and which is the doorway to a Magic regio and a Faerie regio.
quotes: The temenos has both a Magic aura of 3 and a Faerie aura of 3.
At certain times of the year, however, the Faerie aura increases to 4 and suppresses the Magic aura.

entries.title: Bear Island: The Jasonian Way (faerie regio path)
entries.summary: A faerie regio path to the summit of Mount Dindymon with fixed travel time, entrances in weaker or stronger Faerie auras at each end, and a vast faerie forest of Gegenees off the path.
quotes: It takes four hours to travel the trail, no matter what the characters do to expedite this process.

entries.title: Bear Island: Entering the regiones and Regio Sight ease factors
entries.summary: How to enter the Faerie regio by ritual and how to find either regio by spell or Regio Sight roll, with Ease Factors that change depending on which aura currently dominates.
quotes: Under the Temenos of Dindyméné's Magic aura, the Ease Factor to see the Magic regio is 11 and to see the Faerie regio is 23.
When the temenos has a Faerie aura of 4, the Ease Factor to see the Magic regio is 25 and to see the Faerie regio is 9.

entries.title: Bear Island: Faerie Regio of Dindyméné
entries.summary: The Faerie regio behind the temenos, home of the Idaian Daktyls, stacked with a Magic aura and Magic regio.
quotes: The Faerie regio has a Faerie aura of 6.

entries.title: Bear Island: Magic Regio of Dindyméné
entries.summary: An enlarged, uninhabited Magic regio whose peace gives visitors a temporary Calm personality trait unless they have Magic-realm supernatural abilities, and which grows Herbam and Terram vis each year.
quotes: With a Magic aura of 6, the Magic regio is an enlarged copy of the Temenos of Dindyméné.
Entering characters gain a new Personality Trait, Calm +2, unless they have supernatural abilities derived from the Magic realm, which includes the Gift.

entries.title: Cursewood: The Regio (entry only when led by Wyzwanie)
entries.summary: The level 7 Magic regio containing Regulus' encampment, which may be entered only if the spirit allows it by letting the worthy cross the wall.
quotes: Regulus' encampment is now hidden in a Magic regio of level 7.

entries.title: Farne Islands: Inner Farne (Divine aura and miraculous barley vis)
entries.summary: A Divine aura island with a miraculous spring and a one-month barley crop from which Creo vis can be harvested if the grain can be ripened supernaturally fast and protected from the magical birds.
quotes: Divine aura 2, rising to 4 in the chapel.

entries.title: Farne Islands: The Wideopens (gut hazard and tunnel regio)
entries.summary: Unconsecrated burials make the dead vulnerable to necromancy, a gut needs ship handling rolls in bad weather, and a tunnel inside a Magic aura 2 regio opens only occasionally.
quotes: a ship handling roll must be made every 100 paces in all but the calmest of weathers

entries.title: Farne Islands: The Bush (surviving immersion by faith)
entries.summary: A character of strong faith stranded here suffers no ill effects and can survive the tidal immersion by praying with a Stamina + Concentration roll; a year here can form part of a Test of Faith.
quotes: If he prays during the hour that the island is totally immersed (requiring a Stamina + Concentration roll of Ease Factor 6) then he can survive without air to breathe.

related.text: Realms of Power: the Divine p.59 Test of Faith

entries.title: Tartaran Regiones
entries.summary: A summary of the effects of hellfire in Tartaran regiones: no Fatigue recovery, added fire damage, and a damage bonus based on the victim's sinful Traits.
quotes: No Fatigue levels can be recovered within the regio, and all Fatigue levels lost are Long-Term Fatigue.
Add sum of the sinful Personality Traits to all fire or heat Damage Totals, counting negative virtuous traits as sinful.

related.text: Realms of Power: the Infernal p.16 Tartaran regiones

versions.title: Tartaran Regiones
versions.summary: Regiones of hellfire: Fatigue becomes long-term, metal burns, flames do heavy fire damage, and sinful Personality Traits increase fire damage taken.
quotes: The flames, if touched directly, do anywhere from +5 to +35 fire damage

entries.title: Celestial Regiones
entries.summary: A summary of the effects of Celestial regiones on visitors: a stress roll to act normally, Fatigue loss over time, Warping, and the resulting Ascent.
quotes: To act normally, a visitor must make a Stamina + Dominion Lore stress roll against an Ease Factor equal to (3 x aura).
Characters can spend 1 Faith Point to automatically succeed on the roll.

related.text: Realms of Power: the Divine pp.14-15 Celestial regiones
Realms of Power: the Divine p.63 Ascension

versions.title: Celestial Regiones
versions.summary: Describes celestial regiones as unfixed spiritual realms of angels, entered mainly by invitation.

entries.title: Entering the Truffle Regio
entries.summary: How characters find and enter the truffle regio: it needs a guide or exact location, one character able to see the regio, and a local Magic aura that only exists on the solstices and equinoxes. Leaving is possible at any time.
quotes: The Magic aura outside of the regio is 1, only on the solstices and equinoxes, which means that the players must roll against an Ease Factor of 9 to see inside.

related.text: ArM5 p.189 entering and leaving regiones
ArM5 p.158 Piercing the Magical Veil

entries.title: Truffle Regio, first level (Regio Entrance)
entries.summary: Describes the outermost level of the regio, its Magic aura, how to spot the path leading onward, and how the Wild Boar of the Woods intercepts intruders and sends them after interloping wolves.
quotes: The first level of the regio has a Magic aura of 3.
With a Hunt + Perception roll against an Ease Factor of 9, the character notices a path leading away from the regio entrance.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.55 Creatures of Virtue

entries.title: Truffle Regio, second level (Truffle Fields)
entries.summary: Describes how to reach the second level of the regio, which has a stronger Magic aura, and what happens if the characters cannot see the way on and loop back to the first level.
quotes: The second level of the regio has a Magic aura of 5.

related.text: ArM5 p.158 Piercing the Magical Veil

entries.title: Truffle Regio, third level (Truffle Holt)
entries.summary: Describes how characters cross into the third and final level of the regio, which has the strongest Magic aura, with help from the truffle workers or by finding the entrance themselves.
quotes: The third and final level of the regio has a Magic aura of 7.

entries.title: Faerie Court Regio
entries.summary: Describes a faerie court regio with a strong Faerie aura, how characters cross into it from the mundane forest, and its endless-looking but finite geography. Useful as a worked example of a faerie regio.
quotes: which is a regio with a Faerie aura of 4

entries.title: Finding a Moving Regio Entrance by Horoscope
entries.requires: A regio whose entrance shifts with sun and moon
entries.summary: A regio whose entrance is the darkest place in a forest moves with the seasons and the heavenly bodies. A character can work out where it will be by casting a horoscope, then needs to be able to see the way in; carrying light defeats the purpose, and an Arcane Connection spell can bypass the entrance.
quotes: Intelligence + Artes Liberales (astronomy) roll against an Ease Factor of 9

related.text: ArM5 p.158 Piercing the Faerie Veil

entries.title: Moving Through Sticky Webs
entries.summary: Webs fill a regio so that any movement, even flying, needs a successful roll. Stuck characters cannot attack or defend, and a botch in melee can leave a free character stuck.
quotes: moving around (including flying) requires a successful Strength + Stress Die roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: The Time Trap (Frozen Time in a Regio)
entries.requires: Regio in which time has been stopped
entries.summary: In a regio where time is frozen, long-Duration spells and effects do not expire, while Momentary spells work as usual. Destroying enough of the web that holds time releases it, aging everything inside and ending short-Duration effects.
quotes: any spells (and other effects) cast with a long Duration in the regio do not expire
everything in the regio ages by one year; make Aging rolls if required

entries.title: Entering a Haunted Infernal Regio and Its Heat and Smoke
entries.requires: Infernal regio (Realms of Power: The Infernal)
entries.summary: An Infernal regio that opens at set times and can be crossed by those who can see into it. Characters who stay inside must make a Deprivation check each Diameter for heat and smoke, with a bonus for covering the face.
quotes: A character who wraps his face in a cloth receives a +3 bonus to the Deprivation roll.

entries.title: The Monsters in the Ironwood
entries.summary: Describes the Ironwood regio: its single-level Magic aura aligned to a giant-derived tradition so only users of that magic gain the aura bonus, its hostile terrain, and the warped Hundings and Muspelli who live there.
quotes: The Ironwood has a single level with a Magic aura of 9.
This aura is aligned to trolldomur (Rival Magic page 92), which means that only those using giant-derived magic can benefit from the aura modifier.

entries.title: The Aggtelek Caves
entries.summary: Gives the auras, vis types and special lesser-enchantment vis of the Aggtelek caves near Laniena, including a ward-granting vis from the iron flowers of Ochtinska Cave.
quotes: Baradla, as the biggest and most spectacular, has the most powerful aura of 5.
Both Imaginem and Muto vis can be collected in Baradla Cave.

entries.title: Ivan Rilski's Cave
entries.summary: Gives the Divine aura of the cave, tree and rock associated with Saint Ivan Rilski, which is separate from the Dominion aura of the nearby monastery.
quotes: The cave, tree, and rock bear a Divine aura of 4, separate from the Dominion aura of 3 possessed by the monastery.

entries.title: The Seven Lakes
entries.summary: Describes the Faerie aura and per-lake regiones of the Seven Lakes and the vila hosts who grant faerie gifts (each equivalent to a Minor Virtue with a Faerie Charm) to guests who accept a deadly year-and-a-day stay.
quotes: The area has a Faerie aura of 3, and each lake has a Faerie regio of aura 6.
Each gift is equivalent to a Minor Virtue, and is accompanied by a Faerie Charm.

entries.title: Starosel Tomb Temple Aura
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura, vis types and guardian genius loci of the Starosel tomb temple as a potential oppidum site.
quotes: it has a strong Magic aura of 6
Both Terram and Herbam vis can be collected within a few yards from the tomb temple.

entries.title: The Madara Horseman
entries.summary: Describes the Faerie aura of the Madara plateau and how a faerie rite wakes the Horseman and his opposing Lion, with a guideline for their Faerie Might.
quotes: The whole plateau has a Faerie aura of 3, which rises to 5 in immediate proximity to the Horseman.
The Madara Horseman should have a Faerie Might of at least 20, although this could be more depending on the needs of the people and the success of the rite which awakens him.

entries.title: Gela
entries.summary: Explains the sanctum at Gela where the resident magus receives an annual personal vis source in return for teaching music and performance.
quotes: In return for an annual grant of vis from the oppidum (amounting to a Personal Vis Source), the magus in residence is obliged to teach music and performance to those who ask.

entries.title: The Devil's Throat
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura of the Devil's Throat cave and the Corpus vis found on the shore of its underground lake.
quotes: There is a Magic aura of 4 here.
Corpus vis that is occasionally washed up on the shores of the underground lake in the form of fragments of ancient skeletons.

entries.title: Perperikon
entries.summary: Describes the Magic aura of the ruined oracular city of Perperikon and the seasonal fertility aura of the Rock Womb, including its use as a source of Insight into Fertility Magics.
quotes: Perperikon has a Magic aura of 3.
the Rock Womb becomes flooded with a powerful Magic aura aligned with fertility.

entries.title: Seuthopolis Caverns and Auras
entries.summary: Gives the aura of the Thracian caverns beneath Seuthopolis, which house the magi's laboratories and libraries, and the Divine exception in the crypt.
quotes: These have a Magic aura of 5, with a few exceptions, such as the Crypt of the Martyred Virgin, which is Divine.

entries.title: Regiones at Tablinum (access via Arcane Connections)
entries.summary: Explains that Tablinum's many superimposed regiones cannot be entered by sensing or following a path, but only by targeting Fixed Arcane Connections held by the curator with effects such as Leap of Homecoming.
quotes: The Arcane Connections are used to target Leap of Homecoming and similar effects to allow travel to the different regiones.

entries.title: The Empty Halls (empty regiones)
entries.summary: Describes the many vacant regio halls where characters can be imprisoned or marooned, and the typical Magic auras found there.
quotes: Most of the Empty Halls have Magic auras of 3 or 4.

entries.title: The Scholomance Regio and Auras
entries.summary: Describes the Scholomance tower, which sits inside a regio that opens during violent storms and can wander, with a Magic aura in both the valley and the regio and enchantments that garble speech and smear text.
quotes: At such times the regio (which has a Magic aura of 5) lies open and anyone can walk in

entries.title: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls (regio)
entries.requires: Storyguide-placed site in the Black Forest (never found)
entries.summary: A forest-spirit regio whose levels are the seven waterfalls; a visitor may only ascend each level by completing a different Quest, gaining a new level of understanding of the Forest at each step. Gives the spirit's Might, traits and powers as a stat block.
quotes: Magic Might: 50
Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker), Guide, Oath-Swearing, Regio, Shroud

related.text: Realms and Forest Paths in the Rhine Tribunal

entries.title: The Fane of the Founders
entries.summary: A hidden glade with a Magic aura in which twelve magi renew the Oath of the Founders every seven years; the stone is treated as an artifact with Magic Might and a limited set of forest powers, and it yields vis to those who perform the rite.
quotes: Thus, the Fane may be treated as if it has a Magic Might of 40
Produce Vis, Shroud, Oath-Swearing, Grant Virtue (Clear Thinker; temporarily)

related.text: The Glade of the Seven Waterfalls

entries.title: The Source of the Danube (Faerie regio)
entries.requires: Storyguide-placed site in the eastern Black Forest
entries.summary: An enchanted spring and bottomless pool with a Faerie aura that rises within the water and in the deeper levels of a regio, ending in a gateway to Arcadia; large amounts of Aquam vis can be harvested at the cost of angering the river spirit.
quotes: There is a Faerie aura of 3 in the region of the pool, which rises to 5 if one is within the water itself.

entries.title: The Brocken: Faerie aura that doubles on Walpurgis Night
entries.requires: Visit to the Brocken in the Harz
entries.summary: A potent supernatural mountain where the Faerie aura varies by altitude and doubles on Walpurgis Night; also a source of a vis plant, a vision-granting spring and a place to find potential apprentices.
quotes: The lower slopes of the Brocken have a Faerie aura of 2, with 4 at the summit. These values are doubled on Walpurgis Night.

entries.title: The Feengrotten (shifting caves yielding Imaginem vis)
entries.summary: A faerie-touched cave network with a weak Magic aura whose passages shift; only those who are genuinely lost for days emerge covered in Imaginem vis dust, while anyone trying to exploit the property gets plain dust.
quotes: The Feengrotten has a Magic aura of 1.
the dust is Imaginem vis, the quantity dependent on how many days that they were lost

entries.title: Irencillia: Shifting Appearance and Patchy Faerie Aura
entries.summary: Faerie glamour makes the covenant look and feel different to each visitor, with sancta and communal areas settling into a firm consensus reality. Its Faerie aura varies from place to place, with the strongest patches (some inside regiones) holding the magi's sancta.
quotes: The Faerie aura of Irencillia is highly patchy.
All areas within the boundary wall have an aura of at least 1

entries.title: Fenistal: A Single-Level Magic Regio
entries.summary: The exsules' hidden base lies in the upper level of a Magic regio from which all intermediate levels have been removed by powerful magic, making it very hard to reach.
quotes: with a Magic aura of 8

entries.title: Brocéliande (Faerie Forest, Auras and Vis Sources)
entries.summary: The Faerie forest of Brocéliande with its aura levels, the Fountain of Youth, the Stone of Merlin, Lake Comper's Faerie regio and the vis available from its lake, bridge and Barenton fountain.
quotes: Most of the forest has a Faerie aura of level 2 and there are places where it is considerably higher.

related.text: Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal p.38 Path of Aging

entries.title: Carnac (Magic by Day, Infernal by Night)
entries.summary: The great stone avenues of Carnac, one of the strongest Magic auras known, which turns Infernal at night and is haunted by the Nains, with notes on research there and its many regiones.
quotes: By day, a Magic aura of strength 5 covers the heath
As the shadows lengthen the Magic aura fades away, and at night an Infernal aura replaces the magic.

entries.title: Mont St. Michael (Tidal Divine Regio)
entries.summary: The abbey is a Divine regio at high tide that nobody can enter or leave, with only an ordinary Divine aura at low tide; also covers its history as a former druidic site whose Magic aura was destroyed.
quotes: the monastery has a Divine aura of only 4

entries.title: Oleron: The Apple Mile Faerie Regio
entries.summary: Describes a covenant regio with a strong Faerie aura and perpetual summer, whose roads loop back on themselves and lead only to the mortal world and the Stone Couches.
quotes: Within the regio, which has a Faerie aura of 5, it is always summer.

entries.title: Lapis Crudus: Regio Gate and Social Status Swap
entries.summary: Describes the sealed Faerie regio containing the covenant and the mirror-hut gate through which people can cross only by exchanging places with someone of comparable Social Status, along with the regio's Faerie aura and vis sources.
quotes: The persons must have comparable (but not necessarily identical) Social Status Virtues or Flaws to effect the passage to or from the regio
Within the regio, the covenant sits in a Faerie aura of 7.

entries.title: Cunfin: Magic Regio Within a Divine Aura
entries.summary: A covenant sits in a Magic regio overlapping a monastery's strong Divine aura, a coexistence nobody can explain, with a single-level regio entered by anyone carrying a charm made from stones of the old fort.
quotes: The regio's single level can be accessed by anyone holding a charm made from the stones of the fort.

entries.title: Cunfin: Holy Influence Calming the Dominion, Mercere Portal
entries.summary: Describes how a magus with Holy Influence shapes the temper of the surrounding Dominion to reduce conflict with mundanes, that the magi's Gentle Gift eases dealings with locals, and that the covenant hosts a Mercere Portal.
quotes: Eloi uses his Holy Influence to give the Dominion surrounding the monastery a Calm temper

entries.title: Confluensis Magical Resources and Local Auras
entries.summary: Describes the covenant's strong Magic aura, the tidal vortices harvested for vis on spring tides, and the Orchard island whose aura has shifted from Faerie to Magic with a minor Faerie aura returning on the solstices.
quotes: The island's aura, once Faerie, has gradually been transformed to Magic, although a minor Faerie aura reappears on the solstices.

entries.title: The Cave of the Seven Sleepers (dilated-time regio)
entries.requires: Location: Cave of the Seven Sleepers, near Ephesus
entries.summary: A Divine-aura pilgrimage cave that still hides a Magic regio with dilated time, tempting vis harvesters who cannot predict how much time will pass outside.
quotes: It has a Magic aura of 6 and has dilated time (Covenants, page 7).

entries.title: Lost Temple of Ramses (Faerie regio)
entries.summary: Describes a hidden Faerie regio holding twin temples, its aura strength, and the baboon ritual that reveals the way in.
quotes: Explorers have been unsuccessful in locating the lost temples because they reside within a Faerie regio with an aura of 5.

entries.title: Tumulus Graves (Magic aura)
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura strength of intact Nobatian royal tumuli and notes the grave guardians that may protect them.
quotes: Each intact tumulus (for some have been robbed) has a Magic aura of 1, and may contain a grave guardian such as a mummified dog.

entries.title: Dju Wa'ab (Magic aura)
entries.summary: Gives the Magic aura of the sacred mountain Dju Wa'ab, hints that the surrounding burial sites are stronger, and notes the faded Faerie auras of the old temples.
quotes: Dju Wa'ab, as an impressive natural feature, has a Magic aura of 3; the various burial sites might have a higher aura.

entries.title: Kurru (Magic aura)
entries.summary: The first Kushite pyramid field carries a Magic aura from two centuries of use as a royal cemetery.
quotes: There is a Magic aura of 2 at Kurru, deriving from the use of this site for two centuries.

entries.title: Nuri Necropolis (Magic aura)
entries.summary: The later Napatan pyramid field has a strong Magic aura earned by about five hundred years of use as a royal cemetery.
quotes: Nuri was in use for about five hundred years, before Arqamani moved the royal cemetery to Meroë, long enough for it to gain a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: The Church of the Granite Columns (Dominion auras)
entries.summary: Gives the Dominion aura strengths of Dongola's cathedral and the neighbouring Church of the Angels.
quotes: There is a Dominion aura of 7 within the cathedral.

entries.title: Ancient Auras
entries.requires: Saga set among ancient Egyptian or Nubian monuments
entries.summary: Explains how long-used ancient cemeteries and monuments gain Magic auras after their Faerie auras fade, and how natural features or decay modify the strength.
quotes: These tethers have generated a Magic aura of 1 for every century that they saw continuous use

entries.title: Kerma Cemetery (Magic auras)
entries.summary: Gives the graded Magic aura levels across the huge royal tumuli and the rest of the ancient Kerma cemetery.
quotes: A Magic aura of level 3 lingers around these four tumuli, but weakens to 2 over the rest of the royal cemetery and 1 over the rest of the graves.

entries.title: El-Hobagi (Faerie aura)
entries.summary: The tumulus and temple of Atum at el-Hobagi, with a Faerie aura around the temple and notes on entering the unopened tumulus.
quotes: The Faerie aura of 3 at the temple suggests that the building is still used for worship of the Kushitic gods

entries.title: Begarawiyah Necropolis (Magic auras)
entries.summary: Gives Magic aura strengths for each cemetery of the royal necropolis outside Meroe, based on centuries of royal burial, and notes occupied pyramids with stronger auras.
quotes: There is a Magic aura of 4 here, representing the preternatural tether of over four hundred years of royal burials.
The preternatural tether of six and a half centuries of royal burials has resulted in a Magic aura of 5.

entries.title: The Lost Regio of the Great Stelae
entries.summary: Describes a Faerie regio of the ancient afterlife reached through the Axum stelae, accessible only when the Divine aura recedes at the winter solstice, and the ghosts of kings who dwell there.
quotes: on the night of the winter solstice, the Divine recedes just enough for Faerie to emerge for one short window, allowing easier entry to the regio within.

entries.title: Ethiopian Church Forests and Tabot (Divine auras)
entries.summary: Explains how the sacred forest around an Ethiopian church concentrates its Divine aura, how a lush forest strengthens it, and how the consecrated tabot maintains the aura.
quotes: In communities with these forests, the Divine aura is concentrated within the forest area, resulting in an aura one lower in the areas outside the forest, even if the church is in the middle of town.

related.text: Realms of Power: Divine Revised p.10

entries.title: True Faith
entries.summary: True Faith is measured by a Score and Faith Points that work like Confidence, and the Score gives Magic Resistance; Faith Points are regained each dawn up to the Score.
quotes: TRUE FAITH MAGIC RESISTANCE: True Faith Score X 10
Each dawn, you regain a number of Faith Points up to your True Faith Score

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, p.56

alsoIn.title: Taking the True Faith Virtue (Faith Score and Points)

versions.title: True Faith (overview)
versions.summary: Explains what True Faith is, who can hold it, and that it is represented by a Major Virtue, a True Faith Score and Faith Points. A character with it can pray for miracles and gains magical resistance, and on death is invested with Divine Might.
quotes: invested with Divine Might (equal to his True Faith Score multiplied by 10)
Only living people may have True Faith.

entries.title: Example of Creating a Devout Character
entries.requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious
entries.summary: A worked example of assigning starting Devotion Points to saints for a pious lay character, including the extra Devotion Points a relic can grant.

entries.title: Devotion
entries.requires: Christian character with a positive Personality Trait: Pious (or the Pious Personality Flaw)
entries.summary: Introduces Devotions to particular saints as a Divine-aligned Ability-like statistic bought with separate Devotion Points rather than ordinary experience, and gives the character-generation rule for how many Devotions and Devotion Points a pious Christian starts with.
quotes: Devotions advance as an Ability, but do not use normal, generalized Experience Points, instead relying on a dedicated form of experience points called Devotion Points.
may spend Devotion Points equal to the positive score in that trait to establish Devotions

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

versions.title: Devotion (True Faith 2)
versions.summary: At the stated Score the character gains Premonitions and can dispel any supernatural illusion or Faerie glamour by spending a Faith Point.
quotes: the character may dispel any supernatural (magical and Infernal) illusion or Faerie glamour, no matter its level, by spending a Faith Point

entries.title: The Benefits of Devotion
entries.summary: A Devoted character can invoke any saint he has Devotion in; the Devotion score is added to the invocation roll. Also explains sacramentals as ordinary invocations of an appropriate saint, which avoid the unknown-saint penalty.
quotes: Communication + Charm + modifiers + a simple die vs. 15 + a simple die
the –15 penalty for invoking an unknown saint is not applied

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87 Invoking a saint

entries.title: Relics & Devotion
entries.requires: Possession of a relic of a saint
entries.summary: A carried or tended relic of a saint adds to the Devotion Total when asking that saint to intercede, once a day, and also removes the unfamiliar-saint penalty.
quotes: Relic Bonus: (Faith Points in relic) x 2 bonus to Devotion Total

entries.title: The Costs of Devotion
entries.summary: A Devoted character must observe the saint's feast day each year, losing the day for seasonal activities, and loses Devotion Points if he fails to do so.
quotes: A character failing to celebrate the festival of his saint in some manner will lose at least three Devotion Points

entries.title: Gaining Devotion Points
entries.summary: Lists the activities that earn Devotion Points in play (seasons of prayer, endowing churches, guild membership, shrine visits, sponsoring art, studying hagiographies, advancing the saint's cultus, witnessing miracles, processions, pilgrimage, visions) and the usual award for each.
quotes: Spending a season engaged in prayer and meditation at a shrine to a saint earns 5 Devotion Points.
grants a number of Devotion Points equal to the Aesthetic Quality of the final artwork
worth Devotion Points equal to Quality/2

related.text: The Church Ch.3 Petitioning the Church

entries.title: False Devotion
entries.summary: Devotion can be directed at an unrecognised saint or even a mistaken entity of another realm without heresy, because dulia is not worship; true worship (latria) of anything but God is a serious sin.

entries.title: Experiencing Divine Ascent
entries.summary: A Divine-aligned character who gains enough Warping Points in a single event rolls to resist Divine Ascent, and on a failure undergoes Divine Form (contemplatives) or Divine Gloom (monistics) and takes extra Warping Points equal to the margin of failure.
quotes: Presence + Concentration (or Meditation) + Stress die vs. Warping Score + Warping Points gained + True Faith Score local aura + stress die (no botch)

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.63 Divine Ascent

entries.title: Divine Warping and the Contemplative Mystic
entries.requires: Contemplative mystic who has suffered Divine Form
entries.summary: Summarizes the permanent changes of Divine Form for a contemplative mystic: added Magic Resistance, a Soak bonus, a Penetration bonus, extra botch dice for impious acts, automatic wounds for sin and a continuous Commanding Aura.
quotes: The character gains a Penetration Bonus equal to her Warping Score, with an additional bonus equal to her (True Faith Score multiplied by 5).
The character gains a bonus to physical Soak totals equal to the Magic Resistance Total divided by 5

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.64 Divine Form

entries.title: Divine Warping and the Monistic Mystic
entries.requires: Monistic mystic who has suffered Divine Gloom
entries.summary: Summarizes Divine Gloom for a monistic mystic: Warping Points convert into experience in Dominion Lore and Holy Abilities at the cost of mundane Ability experience, with a bonus against Celestial Disorientation and attraction of supernatural beings.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.63 Divine Gloom
Realms of Power: The Divine p.14 Celestial Disorientation

entries.title: Improving True Faith
entries.summary: True Faith can only be gained or raised through a story and a troupe decision, and higher scores grant extra abilities such as dispelling illusions, doubled Magic Resistance against Mentem, and an Empyreal Aura.
quotes: At True Faith 3, the character gains double Magic Resistance against Mentem spells and similar supernatural powers, and adds +6 instead of +3 to a die roll for each Faith Point spent.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.56-63 True Faith
Realms of Power: The Divine p.12 Empyreal Aura

entries.title: Templars Calling on God's Aid
entries.summary: Templars routinely petition God's aid before battle, led by a brother-priest or, lacking one, the commanding Templar, using the Divine rules for calling on God's aid.
quotes: The Templar commander (or ranking Templar) may also call on God's aid if there is no brother-priest.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.41-42

entries.title: Invocation (Holy Method)
entries.summary: The Holy Method of calling on God's power with spoken or written prayer, costing Confidence or Faith and optionally using a stress die.
quotes: This adds Communication to your roll, and requires that you spend a point of Confidence (or Faith) to bring the effect into being.

entries.title: Meditation (Holy Method)
entries.summary: The Holy Method of achieving ecstasy through chanting or performance, with periodic Stamina rolls and a defence against Divine Ascent.
quotes: you must make a Stamina roll every ten minutes against an Ease Factor of 6
You may subtract your score in Meditation from your roll to avoid Divine Ascent

entries.title: Purity (Holy Method)
entries.summary: The Holy Method of working miracles through strenuous effort, and the rule for extending any holy ritual over hours, days or weeks to spend more Confidence or Faith.
quotes: You must engage in an activity that is strenuous enough to cause you to lose a long-term Fatigue level or suffer a Light Wound, and you use your Stamina for your effect roll.

entries.title: Adjuration (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of summoning, controlling and banishing supernatural creatures, and how Invocation and Purity apply to it.

entries.title: Blessing (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of protecting and aiding a target by dedicating it to God, and how Invocation and Meditation apply to it.

entries.title: Cursing (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of bringing ruin on God's enemies, and how Invocation and Purity differ in the curses they produce.

entries.title: Intervention (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of making God's will visible in the physical world through signs, transformations and healing, and how Meditation and Purity apply to it.

entries.title: Transcendence (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of overcoming the limits of body and mind, including spiritual travel, and how Meditation and Purity apply to it.

entries.title: Understanding (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of receiving holy visions and hidden knowledge, including the risk of confusion on repeated questions.

entries.title: Wonders (Holy Power)
entries.summary: The Power of conjuring items, creatures and forces of nature through Invocation, and what happens on a tragedy of hubris.

entries.title: Who Can Have True Faith?
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling on who is eligible for True Faith: infernalists, devotees of pagan gods, Criamon followers of the Enigma and animals cannot have it, though some monotheistic pagan philosophers might.
quotes: Since infernalists and those aligned with the Infernal Realm are in a deep state of sin, they may not have True Faith.

entries.title: Gaining True Faith During Play
entries.summary: True Faith cannot be taught, learned or gained by initiation; it may be gained in play through a quest or the climax of a major story, never with a guaranteed outcome.
quotes: True Faith does not have a corresponding ability, it may not be taught or learned

entries.title: Playing a Character With True Faith
entries.summary: Describes how True Faith protects the character: it cannot be targeted, detected, suppressed or altered by magic or supernatural powers, has no ceiling on its Score, and does not require being a Mythic Companion.
quotes: True Faith may not be targeted by magic or by the powers of supernatural creatures, and may not be detected, suppressed, or altered through Intellego, Perdo, or Rego spells.

entries.title: Tests of Faith and Crises of Faith
entries.summary: God tests those with True Faith through trials; during a test the character may not spend Faith Points or use Holy Virtues. Sidebars advise on using tests as story hooks, and the text describes the crisis of faith when True Faith is lost.
quotes: In game terms, the character may no longer spend Faith Points or use Holy Virtues for the duration of the test.

entries.title: Crisis of Faith (story uses)
entries.summary: During a crisis of faith the character loses Faith Points and holy powers fail, with no set duration or recovery task; used as a story device to regain or lose True Faith.
quotes: During a crisis of faith, the character loses his Faith Points, prayers remain unanswered, and none of his holy powers work.

entries.title: True Faith and Personality
entries.summary: Spending Faith Points like Confidence is how purification shows in game terms, and saintly characters should have complementary Personality Traits; gaining a sinful trait may trigger a crisis of faith.
quotes: gaining a sinful Personality Trait may result in a crisis of faith

entries.title: Saintly Reputation
entries.summary: Miracles raise a saintly character's Reputation quickly, and a character with a True Faith Score cannot gain a negative Reputation.
quotes: Each miracle he successfully prays for counts as one noteworthy action per Faith Point he possesses, so long as there was a witness.

entries.title: Praying for Miracles
entries.summary: To pray for a miracle, a character with a Faith Point picks an effect, spends the point and rolls against the power's level; Faith Points can boost the roll, groups may pray together, and miracles have infinite Penetration.
quotes: PRAYING FOR A MIRACLE: True Faith Score + Concentration + Aura + Stress Die
Faith Points may be spent to increase this roll, adding +3 for each point spent
Miracles have an infinite Penetration: a successful miracle transcends all other powers.

entries.title: Miraculous Special Effects
entries.summary: Miracles are usually slow and subtle; asking for faster or more trivial results raises the miracle's level by a modifier.
quotes: Add the modifier to the miracle's level.

entries.title: Miracle Timeliness modifiers
entries.summary: Table of level modifiers for how quickly a miracle manifests after the prayer, from immediate to a generation.
quotes: Immediate (instantly to a few hours): +10
Generation (not longer than fifteen years): –20

entries.title: Miracle Need modifiers
entries.summary: Level modifiers reflecting how desperate, deserving or righteous the prayer is, from calamitous need to impious requests.
quotes: Calamitous (supplicant or the subjects of the prayer are in desperate personal need, such assault from supernatural forces): –15
Impious (supplicant is a pagan, infidel, or unbeliever, or the request is motivated by sin, such as pride or greed): +20

entries.title: Botching a Prayer
entries.summary: A botched prayer costs the character their Faith Points for a time, or blocks all prayers and saint invocations if they had none; it may also provoke a tragedy of hubris.
quotes: Botching a prayer roll results in the temporary loss of all Faith Points for a number of weeks equal to botches scored.

entries.title: Storyguiding Miracles
entries.summary: Advice that miracles are negotiated between player and storyguide before the roll, with the storyguide having final say, to avoid overshadowing magi; failed rolls may bring lesser aid.
quotes: God's hand cannot be forced, even by a lucky roll.

entries.title: Embodying the Light
entries.summary: Introduces the cumulative holy-light powers (Devotion, Hope, Charity) a character gains as their True Faith Score rises.
quotes: These powers are cumulative and are gained when the character gains the appropriate True Faith score.

entries.title: Hope (True Faith 3)
entries.summary: At the stated Score Faith Points spent like Confidence add more, and Magic Resistance against Mentem spells and similar powers is doubled.
quotes: adds 6 instead of 3 when spending Faith Points like Confidence
His Magic Resistance against Mentem spells (and similar supernatural powers) is doubled.

entries.title: Charity (True Faith 5)
entries.summary: At the stated Score the character radiates a Divine Empyreal aura of Voice range whose rating depends on the True Faith Score.
quotes: radiates a tangible Divine Empyreal aura (see Heaven and Earth, Divine Auras) with a rating equal to his True Faith Score minus 4

entries.title: The Divine Ascent (overview)
entries.summary: Holy mystics undergo a unique form of Warping, the Divine Ascent, in one of three forms (Gloom, Form, Unity) that replace the normal Effects of Warping; there is no final Ascent, and characters with only True Faith get generic Warping.
quotes: which replace the normal "Effects of Warping" rules

entries.title: Divine Ascension roll
entries.summary: When a holy character gains two or more Warping Points from one event they roll to resist being lifted into the Divine; failure triggers a form of the Ascent and extra Warping Points equal to the margin of failure.
quotes: DIVINE ASCENSION: Presence + Concentration (or Meditation) + stress die vs. Warping Score + Number of Warping Points Gained + True Faith Score + local aura + stress die (no botch)

entries.title: Experiencing the Ascent (duration)
entries.summary: Describes the visionary experience of the Ascent, how long it lasts (in days, later months), True Faith shortening it, and what happens to the character's body meanwhile.
quotes: BASE ASCENT TIME: (Warping Score + Warping Points gained) in days
A character with True Faith subtracts his Faith Score from the total (although the minimum remains 1 day).

entries.title: Divine Gloom
entries.summary: The Gloom form trades mundane knowledge for holy understanding: Warping Points convert into experience in holy Abilities while an equal amount is lost from mundane Abilities, and the character attracts Invisible World beings.
quotes: The character must lose the same number of Experience Points that he gained from Warping from Abilities with a mundane focus

entries.title: Divine Form
entries.summary: The Form variant makes the character a commanding, near-angelic presence with Magic Resistance and Penetration from Warping Score and Faith, but sinful acts bring extra botch dice and wounds.
quotes: The character's Penetration is equal to his Warping Score, and gains an additional bonus equal to his Faith Score multiplied by 5.
a number of additional botch dice equal to the character's Warping Score multiplied by three

entries.title: Divine Unity
entries.summary: The Unity variant makes the character personify one virtue, boosting a matching Personality Trait by Warping Score and exerting Holy Influence on those nearby and on the aura's Temper.
quotes: The Warped character adds his Warping Score to a Personality Trait determined by the virtue he is personifying

entries.title: The Virtues (for Divine Unity)
entries.summary: Reference list of Christian moral and theological virtues a Divine Unity character may personify.

entries.title: Islamic Virtues (for Divine Unity)
entries.summary: Additional Islamic virtues suitable for a character experiencing Divine Unity.

entries.title: Holy Music (Ability)
entries.summary: Supernatural Ability tied to the Holy Method of Meditation: the character sings a devotional song, rolling Presence + Music against an ease factor, and uses Presence to determine the effect; distractions require a Concentration roll.
quotes: You must sing a devotional song, rolling your Presence + Music vs. an ease factor based on the circumstances.

related.text: Instruments of God, Holy Methods and Traditions

entries.title: Invoking Muslim Holy Forbears (Baraka)
entries.requires: Muslim character in a Dominion setting
entries.summary: Muslims seek baraka from venerated figures by reusing the Christian saint-invocation mechanics, with changes: they must be at the figure's shrine, may always invoke the Qur'an, and never threaten forbears.
quotes: Muslim characters may attempt to invoke baraka from holy forbears using the same mechanics as those given above for invoking Christian saints
Muslims may always invoke the power of the Qur'an, no matter where they are.
Muslims never threaten their holy forbears.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Mythic Christianity, Saints

entries.title: Muslim Invocation Modifiers Table
entries.summary: Table of situational modifiers applied to a Muslim's attempt to invoke baraka from a holy forbear, covering Personality Trait, aura, feast days, relics, donations, peril and sins.
quotes: Highest Muslim Personality Trait | + value of the Trait
No zakat paid within a year | –3

entries.title: Khawass al-Qur'an (Invoking the Qur'an)
entries.summary: The Qur'an itself acts as a holy figure that can be invoked anywhere, using the same method as a forbear, to gain earthly benefits from recitation.
quotes: In game terms, the Qur'an itself may be invoked in the same way as a forbear, in an attempt to gain earthly benefits.

entries.title: The Great Pestilence: Overview and Order of Forms
entries.summary: Overview of the Great Pestilence creature's attack pattern: the order in which Forms are infected, what happens to vis, creatures and auras during each month, and how a ruined Form stops working for Hermetic spellcasting without vis.
quotes: The order of Forms attacked is Herbam, Corpus, Mentem, Vim, Aquam, Auram, Animal, Imaginem, Terram, and finally Ignem.
It takes four months to destroy a Form.

entries.title: Accidentally Creating the Great Pestilence in the Lab
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a player magus trigger the Great Pestilence by a botch or a 9 on the Extraordinary Results Chart while experimenting with Rego Herbam lab work, with a Disaster roll deciding whether a vestige forms.
quotes: the player must roll either a botch or a 9 on the Extraordinary Results Chart
if the roll is anything else (3 or higher) the vestige and the Great Pestilence are created

entries.title: Great Pestilence Penetration vs Magic Resistance
entries.summary: Explains how the Great Pestilence overcomes the Magic Resistance of Magic beings: its powers cost no Might, and its Penetration total is built from its Might and Penetration with bonuses for attacking from the Magic Realm and its current Form province.
quotes: its total Penetration is its Might (50) + its Penetration (10) = 60
for a Penetration total of 80

entries.title: Warning Signs: Premonitions and Visions
entries.summary: Characters with Premonitions or Visions get vague warnings of the coming Great Pestilence, with the accuracy of a Premonitions roll set by thresholds on the result.
quotes: A 6 or higher indicates something terrible is coming
a 15 or higher that a wizard created the malady that will destroy the world

entries.title: Rotting Vis: The Moon of Herbam Rot
entries.summary: First month of infection: all vis of the targeted Form rots, can be noticed by Awareness rolls, still works but makes casting that Form riskier, and can be saved only by moving it fully outside every Magic aura; infected auras stop producing that vis.
quotes: The average autocrat's Ease Factor is 9, while a lazy autocrat's Ease Factor is 12.
Herbam spell-casting requires a stress die in situations that normally use a simple die
It must be outside all Magic auras to retain its potency.

entries.title: Sickness of Magic Creatures: The Moon of Herbam Sickness
entries.summary: Second month of infection: Magic beings of the targeted Form inside Magic auras or regiones must pass weekly Disease Avoidance rolls or die, can be saved by leaving the aura (risking Acclimation), and their deaths weaken the aura and spoil their vis; familiars are affected too.
quotes: must succeed on a Disease Avoidance roll
add one-fourth of their Might to the area's Magic aura, measured in magnitudes

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Acclimation

entries.title: The Great (Form) Pestilence (Disease)
entries.summary: Disease statistics and symptoms for the Great Pestilence as it afflicts creatures, objects, minerals and plants of the attacked Form.
quotes: Critical Phlegmatic Disease, Severity 21 Stable: 12, Improve: 18, Interval: Day

entries.title: Miasmas: The Herbam Miasma Moon
entries.summary: Third month of infection: every Magic aura and regio spawns a drifting invisible miasma that blights things of the attacked Form, lasts a year, has no Might and Penetration Total 0, and penalises Aging rolls for each circulating cycle.
quotes: A miasma has a life span of 1 year.
each miasma penalizes Aging rolls by –2
impose a –2 penalty for every active cycle of Formtype miasmas circulating through Mythic Europe at that time

entries.title: Miasmas and Regiones
entries.summary: Magic regiones generate miasmas that are not blown away and are replaced by newer ones, while Divine, Faerie and Infernal regiones keep miasmas out and act as havens.
quotes: In regiones, and only in regiones, a new miasma will replace an older one.

entries.title: Detecting Miasmas and Aegis Protection
entries.summary: Shows how physicians deduce miasmas from bad air with Intelligence + Medicine, how Second Sight spots one, and that an Aegis of the Hearth keeps foreign miasmas out once the initial one is dealt with.
quotes: Spot a Miasma: Perception + Second Sight + stress die vs. 9
Success is indicated by succeeding on an Intelligence + Medicine roll against an Ease Factor of 9.

entries.title: Handling Multiple Miasmas (Wind and Arrival Tables)
entries.summary: Procedure and wind-direction table for deciding whether, from where and how soon later miasmas reach a locale, using a stress die reduced by the number of Forms infected.
quotes: Roll a stress die (no botch) and subtract the number of Forms infected to determine the number of days before the next miasma visits an area.

entries.title: Slowing the Rate of Infection (Optional Rule)
entries.summary: Optional rule to slow the pace of the Great Pestilence from four months to four seasons per Form for less powerful sagas, stretching the timeline to about ten years.
quotes: Rather than four months to destroy a Form, the Great Pestilence needs four seasons, Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

entries.title: Twilight Tears
entries.summary: After Hellix's accident, every Hermetic Temporary Twilight opens a temporary rent into the Form province the Great Pestilence is currently attacking, which can be seen with a Second Sight or Magical Sensitivity roll and used to enter the Magic Realm.
quotes: Viewing a Twilight Tear: Perception + Second Sight or Magical Sensitivity + stress die vs. 12

entries.title: Marking Time: New Moons and Seasons
entries.summary: Simplified calendar for placing new moons in the seasons over the four years of the Great Pestilence.
quotes: There are 12 new moons per year for the first two years of the Great Pestilence, 13 new moons in the third year, and 12 new moons in the final year.

entries.title: Effect of Destroyed Forms on Supernatural Abilities and Other Traditions
entries.summary: Describes how the rotting Magic Realm raises the difficulty of Magic-realm Supernatural Abilities for each destroyed Form and how to adapt other Magic-based traditions by mapping their divisions to Forms.
quotes: For every destroyed Form, increase the Ease Factor difficulty of every magical Supernatural Ability by 1.

entries.title: Corpus Infection (Corpus Pestilence and Miasma)
entries.summary: Second Form attacked: Corpus vis rots, Corpus beings sicken, and the Corpus miasma infects every human it touches with the lethal Great Corpus Pestilence, while magi and others with Magic Resistance are immune. Covers covenant and city responses, healing aid and the end of unaided Corpus casting.
quotes: Luckily magi, and all others with Magic Resistance, are immune to the
An Intelligence + Medicine roll against an Ease Factor of 6 indicates that relocating and outrunning the miasma are the better options.
This spell grants a sick person a +15 bonus to Recovery rolls.

entries.title: Mentem Infection (Mentem Blight)
entries.summary: Third Form attacked: Mentem miasmas strip people without Magic Resistance of their intellect, replacing Intelligence with Cunning, and the Aging roll penalty from earlier miasmas accumulates.
quotes: Aging rolls are penalized by a cumulative –4
Substitute Cunning for Intelligence to those affected.

entries.title: Vim Infection (Vim Blight)
entries.summary: Fourth Form attacked: Vim vis rots and can no longer be extracted from Magic auras, and Vim miasmas cancel spells and enchanted effects up to a stated level unless protected by the Parma Magica.
quotes: From this point onwards magi cannot extract vis from Magic auras
It cancels any spell or spell-like effect of level 30 or less.

entries.title: Aquam Infection (Aquam Blight and Rain Clouds)
entries.summary: Fifth Form attacked: Aquam miasmas poison and destroy water, small springs are lost for good while large rivers refill, and a covenant can get drinking water by pulling rain clouds to the ground.
quotes: Rain clouds lie 2,000 to 3,000 paces above, well within Range: Sight

entries.title: Auram Infection (Foul Air)
entries.summary: Sixth Form attacked: Auram miasmas foul the air so that breathers are weakened rather than killed, with a physical-activity penalty, Fatigue loss from exertion and a larger Aging roll penalty from the active miasmas.
quotes: Impose a –6 penalty to Aging rolls.
suffers a –3 penalty on all rolls involving physical activity

entries.title: Animal Infection (Animal Blight)
entries.summary: Seventh Form attacked: Animal miasmas inflict an Incapacitating Wound on every animal they touch, ending the milk and meat supply the survivors rely on, and Animal casting then needs vis.
quotes: This spell-like effect inflicts an Incapacitating Wound on an animal.

entries.title: Imaginem Infection (Imaginem Blight)
entries.summary: Eighth Form attacked: Imaginem miasmas stop objects producing visual images so anyone inside seems invisible and sight inside the cloud is lost, though magi still show an image. Describes the effect on sight and navigation.
quotes: things within a miasma are invisible until the miasma moves on

entries.title: Terram Infection (Terram Blight)
entries.summary: Ninth Form attacked: Terram miasmas strip the topsoil and drop structures into a pit, with simple-roll Ease Factors for collapse by structure size, descent rate of the miasma and a large cumulative Aging roll penalty.
quotes: Wooden buildings and small trees collapse on a simple roll against an Ease Factor of 3.
Aging rolls made this Winter are penalized by a cumulative –10 for 5 active types of miasmas

entries.title: Ignem Infection (Ignem Blight)
entries.summary: Final Form attacked: Ignem miasmas coat everything in frost, dealing damage each round to unprotected people and animals and killing small plants.
quotes: Unprotected men and women take +5 damage per round that they are inside an Ignem miasma.

entries.title: After the Great Pestilence (Postmortem)
entries.summary: Describes the end state after all ten Forms are consumed, including the lingering miasmas and the Living Condition modifier applied to the following Aging rolls.
quotes: The Living Condition penalty is modified by –6 for the next set of Aging rolls in the coming Winter.

entries.title: Bookkeeping the Great Pestilence
entries.summary: Advice on tracking only the nearby auras: record vis produced and resident magic beings, stop vis production once its Form is destroyed, and reduce an aura when a powerful resident creature dies.
quotes: the aura diminishes by 1 for every 4 magnitudes of the being's Might

entries.title: Changing the Order of Plagues (Optional Rule)
entries.summary: Optional variant letting the storyguide reorder the Forms attacked to spare civilization, while keeping Herbam first so the characters can link events to Hellix.
quotes: It is important that the first infection be Herbam, to give the characters a clue to Hellix's involvement.

entries.title: Deducing the Order of Forms Attacked
entries.summary: The Pestilence attacks Forms in the order of Hellix's Art strengths, which a researcher can infer from her lab notes with an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll, easier if she helps.
quotes: The observer must succeed with an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against an Ease Factor of 12.
adjust the Ease Factor of the Intelligence + Magic Theory roll to 6

entries.title: Cutting an Aura's Link to the Magic Realm
entries.summary: Once the Arcane Connection between an aura and the Magic Realm is found it can be destroyed like any Arcane Connection, protecting that site from the Pestilence; severing it removes the preternatural part of the aura, or halves it if the tether split is unknown.
quotes: simply reduce the strength of the aura to half its original strength when the connection is severed

entries.title: After the Great Pestilence: Forms, Auras and Vis Recover
entries.summary: When the Pestilence ends the Forms work normally again without vis, miasmas fade within a year, and auras and regiones gradually resume vis production except those that dropped to zero.
quotes: As soon as the Great Pestilence dies, the ten Hermetic Forms start functioning again normally.

entries.title: Weakening an Aura Through Hermetic Viresculture
entries.summary: Optional interaction with Aura Variation: pawns harvested through Viresculture lower the Yearly Aura Modifier of the aura they grew in.
quotes: Yearly Aura Modifier for Viresculture: – (total pawns / 5)

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.10 Aura Variation

entries.title: Traveling Auras
entries.requires: Being type: Faerie with a power permitting travel
entries.summary: Some powerful faeries carry their glamour with them, transforming the surrounding land to suit their motif; the changes fade as the faerie leaves, but the consequences of human actions remain.
quotes: The changes made when the glamour of the faerie lays over an area are not permanent

entries.title: Aura Conflicts: Faeries in Other Realms' Auras
entries.summary: A faerie in an area dominated by another Realm, without admittance, must draw its glamour back into itself, which limits its powers' Range; with admittance it creates a small pocket of Faerie.
quotes: faerie characters cannot use powers with Ranges greater than Touch until they have been given leave to do so, unless they have Arcane Connections to the targets

entries.title: Gaining Admittance
entries.summary: Lists the traditional ways a faerie gains leave to use its glamour in areas of another Realm: terra nullius, a recognized right, an invitation, agreeing to a code, paying a price, or contesting ownership; covenants require the Aegis of the Hearth token.
quotes: only participation in the Aegis of the Hearth ritual, and possession of one of the tokens this creates, allows a faerie to use its powers without facing the formidable magical resistance common to covenants

entries.title: Keeping Home Wonderful
entries.summary: Three ways a faerie protects its demesne while absent (leave a steward, leave its spiritual anchor, or restrict access to set times) and the aura a visitor finds if a steward is left.
quotes: If they enter an area kept by a steward, then its aura will be (steward's Might/5).

entries.title: Extended Glamour
entries.summary: Power letting a faerie be aware of everything in its domain, with the domain's size set by the faerie's Might Score, and yielding vis each year.
quotes: The faerie's Might score determines the size of area possible: a Room (5–10 Might), a Structure (15–25 Might), or a standard Boundary (30+ Might).
The area controlled by the faerie can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of vis

entries.title: Tinted Auras
entries.requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
entries.summary: Rules for tinting a Faerie aura so that everyone within gains temporary Personality Traits, including the roll, how long tints last and combining tints.
quotes: stress die + Presence + Concentration
In a tinted aura, every character is strangely drawn to things that are associated with the tint, and repelled by things that are not.

entries.title: Tinting an Aura Table
entries.requires: Sympathy Trait (from a Virtue or Faerie Warping)
entries.summary: Table of Ease Factors for tinting a Faerie aura to a given Personality Trait value.

entries.title: Cursewood: Malevolent Infernal aura effects
entries.summary: Lists the game effects of the aura of 5 in the Cursewood, a Malevolent Infernal aura: penalties to wound Recovery, added Damage, extra botch dice on physical activities and reopening of demon-caused wounds.
quotes: Wounds suffer a penalty to Recovery rolls equal to the aura rating of 5 while inside.
All physical activities suffer 5 additional botch dice from the aura; this includes all rolls for trek progress.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.12-14 Malevolent auras

entries.title: Cursewood: De-Corrupting the Vis
entries.summary: Tainted vis stays corrupted, but once the Magic aura dominates again, and after a year free of Infernal influence, newly produced vis is clean.
quotes: After a full year with no Infernal influence, all vis sources are free from corruption.

entries.title: Changing an aura (reducing Infernal, raising Magic)
entries.summary: How a corrupting Infernal aura fades once its focus is removed and the Magic aura dominates, and how a Magic aura can be raised with a yearly stress roll and bonuses from magical activities.
quotes: the Infernal aura drops by 1 after a number of years equal to its strength
A stress roll made once per year against an Ease Factor of 15 is needed for a permanent increase of 1.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.10-11

entries.title: Cursewood variant: Dark Faerie Aura
entries.summary: Variant in which a faerie aura rather than an Infernal one produces the same added botch dice, damage and ability penalties, but these effects must penetrate and use the faerie's Might.
quotes: faerie powers and illusions result in the same effects as the Malevolent Infernal aura in the form of added botch dice, added damage, and penalties to Abilities and magic.

entries.title: Creo-aligned aura of the Truffle Regio
entries.summary: Explains the effects of a Creo-aligned Magic aura: doubled aura bonus for Creo activities, aura added to Recovery rolls, cheaper Might for Creo creatures, instant healing of minor hurts, slowed apparent aging and a Living Conditions bonus for a full year.
quotes: The Magic aura bonus is doubled in the regio for all activities involving Creo.
For each season the character spends in the aura, his apparent age is decreased by one, but does not decrease below 27.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.16 aligned auras

entries.title: Faerie Aura Grown from Faerie Sovereignty of a Fief
entries.requires: Faerie ruler holding a mundane fief
entries.summary: When a faerie queen inherits a mundane fief, a Faerie aura appears across it and strengthens each spring equinox up to a cap, often overlapping existing Dominion or other auras. Includes notes on the fief's heralds and their limits against the Aegis of the Hearth.
quotes: every spring equinox the Faerie aura increases by 1, until it reaches a value of 4

entries.title: The Chapel (Divine aura and relics)
entries.summary: The Divine exhibit is a realia in Divine Lore, filled with holy relics, with a Divine aura that probably overrides any Magic aura underneath.
quotes: The Chapel has a Divine aura of 6.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition pp.43-46

entries.title: Studenica Monastery (Divine aura and saint's oil)
entries.summary: A holy site with a very high Divine aura and a saint with substantial Divine Might whose daily flow of oil can bestow a saint's miracle on an anointed person.
quotes: The Studenica is the most holy site in Serbia and has a Divine aura of 8.
With a Divine Might of 50

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.88 Saints' miracles

entries.title: Relics
entries.summary: Every relic has Faith giving Confidence-like Faith Points and Magic Resistance, a Divine Might limiting uses of its powers, and a power that repels Infernal creatures.
quotes: A relic's Divine Might is equal to the relic's Faith score (or highest Faith score, if more than one applies) multiplied by 10, and the Might Pool is refreshed with every sunrise.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine Revised Edition, pp.88-89

versions.title: Relics
versions.summary: Summarizes how relics work: Faith Score and Faith Points, Magic Resistance for the holder, a Divine Might Score and an aura hostile to the Infernal that damages entering creatures of lesser Might.
quotes: Anyone who holds the relic has a Magic Resistance equal to 10 x the Faith Score
related: Realms of Power: The Divine pp.43-46 Relics

entries.title: Miracles
entries.summary: Miracles are direct divine intervention and cannot fail or be resisted.
quotes: As such, they can do anything, cannot fail, and cannot be resisted by any other power.

entries.title: Becoming a Saint
entries.requires: Troupe decision; character died with the Personality Trait Pious at the required level
entries.summary: Sets out the conditions under which a deceased character may become a genuine saint and, separately, be formally canonised by the Church, and points to the saint-design rules in Realms of Power: The Divine.
quotes: died with a Personality Trait Pious of 6 or higher

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.60-61 Miracles
Realms of Power: The Divine p.89 Designing saints

entries.title: Threatening a Saint
entries.summary: After failing to invoke a saint, a petitioner may threaten him with a Presence + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor based on the saint's Divine Might; Confidence but not Faith Points may be spent.
quotes: You make a Presence + Leadership + modifiers + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9 + one fifth of the saint's Divine Might.
THREATENING A SAINT: Presence + Leadership + modifiers + stress die vs. 9 + Saint's Divine Might/5

entries.title: Threat Modifiers and Outcomes
entries.summary: Table of modifiers for threatening a saint and the results: success grants the miracle, failure bars aid for a month, a big failure brings a minor curse and a season without aid, and a botch brings the curse.
quotes: If your roll is ten or more points beneath the Ease Factor the saint punishes you by inflicting a minor curse

entries.title: Saints' Powers list
entries.summary: List of miracle powers saints can use, each with a Might point cost, initiative modifier and Form, from Acknowledgment of Evil to Tomorrow's Bounty.
quotes: The Penetration of this miracle (Divine Might – (5 x Might Point cost of power))

entries.title: Saints' Curses list
entries.summary: List of curses saints can inflict on those who threaten their followers, each with Might cost, initiative and effect.

entries.title: Designing Saints
entries.summary: Rules for creating a saint: Divine Might by rank (Blessed Virgin, greater, area, local) and a rule of thumb that the saint's powers should cost at most a fifth of its Divine Might.
quotes: GREATER SAINT: Divine Might 75
AREA SAINT: Divine Might 50
LOCAL SAINT: Divine Might 25
Generally, a saint should be given powers whose total point cost to use is less than or equal to one fifth of their Divine Might.

entries.title: Sample Saint (stat template)
entries.summary: Basic statistics template for a saint as a bodiless Divine creature, to which Divine Might and powers are added.
quotes: Characteristics: Int +5, Per +5, Pre +5, Com +5, Str n/a, Stm n/a, Dex n/a, Qik n/a

entries.title: Holy Influence (Rabbis and Chief Rabbis)
entries.requires: Rabbi, Chief Rabbi or Exilarch with spiritual authority
entries.summary: Explains which Jewish leaders hold spiritual authority and may exert Holy Influence, including tempering an aura, and over what area or community each can do so.
quotes: Rabbis have spiritual authority over the auras centered upon and the community served by their synagogue or yeshivah, while Chief Rabbis may extend their influence across their city.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, Chapter Three (tempering auras)

entries.title: Jewish Ritual Objects as Relics
entries.summary: Describes Jewish sacred objects and notes the circumstances in which tefillin and the shofar count as relics with a Faith Point, and when they have no power.
quotes: When it is sounded on a holy day or as part of a Jewish exorcism rite, the shofar is treated as a relic with one Faith Point.
those once owned by one of the Tzadikim Nistarim (see later) act as a relic with one Faith Point.

entries.title: Cracking of Old Wards
entries.summary: As the Dominion rises, old magical wards (such as those holding subdued creatures) weaken individually or in clusters, leaving weak auras that spring covenants may colonize.
quotes: Sites that have contained powerful, subdued magical creatures for centuries are likely to have weak auras and be prime sites for colonization by spring covenants.

entries.title: The Relics of Constantinople (Faith Scores)
entries.summary: Sidebar on the great relics of Constantinople, giving each a Faith Score, powers and the guidance that relics should motivate characters rather than start in play.
quotes: A fragment of the True Cross that is as large as a man's leg has a Faith Score of 10, giving it 10 Faith Points and a Divine Might of 100.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine, page 35 (Powerful Relic)

entries.title: Greek Saints (saint categories and Divine Might)
entries.summary: Sidebar recalling the three categories of saint and their Divine Might, with lists of notable Greater, Area and Local saints of the Greek Church.
quotes: Greater saints have a Divine Might of 75, area saints a Divine Might of 50, and local saints a Divine Might of 25.

entries.title: Ark of the Covenant and Ring of Solomon (relic Faith Scores)
entries.summary: Gives the Faith Scores and Divine Might of the Ark of the Covenant and the Ring of Solomon for different believers, the ring's bonus to Solomonic and Ars Notoria casting, and its use as a tractatus.
quotes: The Ark of the Covenant has a Faith Score of 10, giving it 10 Faith points and a Divine Might of 100 for any Ethiopian, Falasha or Christian

related.text: Realms of Power: Divine Revised pp.44, 98

entries.title: Arcadian Travel (Merinita Mystery) Threshold Charm
entries.summary: A magus with Arcadian Travel builds a charm object or performance, rolls against a set Ease Factor, and on success adds his Arcadian Travel Total as Threshold points, bringing along companions.
quotes: against an Ease Factor of 18
Arcadian Travel Total: stress die + Perception + (Ability used to make the charm) + aura
equal to his Faerie Magic score

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.92 Arcadian Travel

entries.title: New Power: Spirit Away
entries.summary: Faerie power that spends Might to add Threshold points to mortals who already have some, or to send characters out of Faerie.
quotes: at a cost of 1 Might Point per Threshold point
this costs 3 Might Points per character

entries.title: Faerie Adventurers
entries.requires: Being type: Faerie (player or non-player faerie characters)
entries.summary: Faerie characters enter Faerie by the same procedure as mortals but gain Threshold bonuses by cognizance, know which Guardian choice leads in, gain fable points more easily, act as if they have Common Sense, and are immune to Warping on leaving.
quotes: Highly cognizant faeries automatically have a number of Threshold points equal to the magnitude of their Might.
Assume that all faerie characters have the Common Sense Virtue while in the Faerie Realm.

entries.title: The Mother Road
entries.requires: Faerie Portage, or House Merinita Wayfarers
entries.summary: A traveler stepping onto a trod can bargain with the Guardian to enter Faerie and exit at another trod, covering great distances quickly but without gaining fable points and relying on the Guardian for the way out.
quotes: typically one minute passes for every 24 minutes spent in the Faerie Realm

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.80 Wayfarers

entries.title: Leaving Faerie by Merinita Mysteries
